Grisly Gash.name: Grisly Gash
Grisly Gash.description:
Requirements Slaughtermay's previous action was a hook sword Strike that damaged a foe

Effect Slaughtermay twists and then yanks her hook sword, ripping at the flesh of the creature she damaged with a hook sword on her previous action. That creature takes @Damage[(1d6+5)[bleed]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:22|basic] save).

Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
Sneak Attack.description: The creature's Strikes deal an additional 1d6 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

Rupturing Shriek.name: Rupturing Shriek
Rupturing Shriek.description: Velicarn's head unleashes a horrific howl that causes blood to leak out of those who hear it and into his gaping open mouth. All creatures within @Template[emanation|distance:30]{30 feet} must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:28|options:area-effect,inflicts:drained] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 2} on a critical failure) as some of their blood runs from their bodies into Velicarn's maw. Creatures currently taking persistent bleed damage take a –2 circumstance penalty to this saving throw. Velicarn's head regains @Damage[5[healing]] Hit Points for every creature in the area, to a maximum of @Damage[25[healing]] Hit Points, and he can't use Rupturing Shriek again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Rupturing Shriek]]{1d4 rounds}.

Snatch.name: Snatch
Snatch.description: Velicarn's head can Fly at half Speed while he has a Medium or smaller creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} in his talons, carrying that creature along with him.

Consume Flesh.name: Consume Flesh
Consume Flesh.description:
Requirements The ghoul is adjacent to the corpse of a creature that died within the last hour.

Effect The ghoul devours a chunk of the corpse and regains @Damage[5d6[healing]] Hit Points.

It can regain Hit Points from any given corpse only once.

Ghoul Whispers.name: Ghoul Whispers
Ghoul Whispers.description:
Requirements A @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} creature is within the ghoul's reach

Effect The ghoul whispers dark thoughts and vile cravings into the creature's ears. The creature must save against the forbidden cravings curse.

Forbidden Cravings (curse) A creature can still eat and drink while sickened by this curse

Saving Throw @Check[will|dc:26|traits:curse]

Stage 1 carrier with no ill effects (1 day)

Stage 2 @Damage[2d6[void]] damage and the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} until it consumes raw meat (1 day)

Stage 3 as stage 2

Stage 4 as stage 2 unless the target has consumed raw meat in the past 24 hours, then it takes @Damage[4d6[void]] damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} until it consumes raw meat;

Stage 5 if the creature has eaten raw meat in the past 24 hours, it dies and rises as a ghoul, if not, it returns to stage 4

Grave Knowledge.name: Grave Knowledge
Grave Knowledge.description:
Frequency once per hour

Effect The ghoul calls upon knowledge it retains from one creature it has consumed in the past 7 days. The ghoul attempts a skill check using a skill in which the consumed creature was trained (if it's unclear whether the creature was trained, the GM decides). The ghoul is treated as trained with a +18 skill modifier. This takes the same amount of actions or time as usual for the check.

The ghoul can instead automatically learn something specific known by a creature it consumed in the last 7 days, like the location of a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden} treasure or the name of a loved one. The ghoul can do this only once for a given creature, no matter how much of its flesh the ghoul consumed.

Swift Leap.name: Swift Leap
Swift Leap.description: The ghoul jumps up to half its Speed. This movement doesn't trigger reactions.

equipment-Pouch of dozens of different c.name: Pouch of dozens of different colored glass beads

Change of Luck.name: Change of Luck
Change of Luck.description:
Frequency once per day

Trigger A creature within 30 feet of the bone croupier attempts a check but hasn't rolled the check yet

Effect The bone croupier pulls on the threads of luck that bind all things. The target rolls twice, and then the bone croupier decides which result applies. If the bone croupier chooses the lower roll, this is a misfortune effect; if the bone croupier chooses the higher roll, it's a fortune effect; if they're the same, the croupier decides which trait to apply. If this ability is expended, the bone croupier rolls [[/br 2d6 #Recharge Change of Luck]] at the start of each of their turns, recharging the ability if the sum is 7 or 11.

Pick a Card, Any Card.name: Pick a Card, Any Card
Pick a Card, Any Card.description:
Mister Moxie designates an adjacent living creature who must pick a card from his deck of harrow cards. The chosen creature finds a phantasmal duplicate deck of cards in their hand and is compelled by fate to draw a card; it can and must do so even if its hands are full, or it's unable to act. The creature rolls [[/gmr 1d6#suit]] to determine the suit of the card drawn to determine the effect (or if you have a harrow deck handy, have the player draw a card to determine the suit).

1—Hammer: (void) The target becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} for 24 hours.

2—Key: The target becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} for 1 minute and can use the extra action each round to Stride or Strike.

3—Shield: (void) The target becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1}.

4—Tome: (void) The target becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} for 24 hours.

5—Star: (healing, vitality) The target regains @Damage[20[healing,vitality]|shortLabel] HP.

6—Crown: (emotion, mental) The target becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} for 1 minute.

Carrion Angel.name: Carrion Angel
Carrion Angel.publicNotes:
Obscure and profane rites enable a blasphemer to transform a captured angel into an undead monstrosity known as a carrion angel. With their decaying flesh, foul stench of decay, and broken wings crawling with flies, none would mistake a carrion angel for anything but the atrocity they are—that is, unless the carrion angel chooses to cloak themself in a more pleasant, illusory deception. A carrion angel is not controlled by their creator, yet they generally regard their creator as an ally. Most outlast their creators, at which point they seek their own evil agendas in the world.

Similar undead atrocities created via sacrifices of other types of celestials exist, and have similar abilities to the carrion angel. Yet for whatever reason, carrion angels are the most well-known and commonly encountered of these rare horrors.

Blasphemous Choices

The typical carrion angel presented here represents the least powerful of their kind, an undead abomination created through vile rites involving an angel's sacrifice to an evil deity. Yet sometimes, fallen angels seek undeath deliberately—not to avoid immortality, as do so many mortals, but simply to embrace an unwholesome and blasphemous new source of power. These carrion angels are often much more powerful than those who had no choice in their fate.
Carrion Angel.allSaves: +1 status to all saves vs. vitality

+1 Status to All Saves vs. Vitality.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Vitality

Blasphemous Stench.name: Blasphemous Stench
Blasphemous Stench.description: 30 feet. A creature entering or starting its turn in the aura must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:27] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (plus @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} as long as it's sickened on a critical failure). A holy creature takes a –2 status penalty to this saving throw. A creature that succeeds at its save or recovers from being sickened is temporarily immune to blasphemous stench for 1 minute unless it is holy.

Decaying Touch.name: Decaying Touch
Decaying Touch.description: The first time each round that a living creature takes damage from a carrion angel's claw Strike, it must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:30|options:inflicts:drained,inflicts:sickened] save to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1} on a failure (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 2} on a critical failure).

Living Facade.name: Living Facade
Living Facade.description: The carrion angel hides their true appearance behind a potent illusion that makes them appear as they did in life. The carrion angel has an automatic result of 42 on Deception checks and DCs to pass as living. While Living Facade is in effect, the carrion angel loses void healing and can be healed as if they were alive. This illusion lasts until the start of the carrion angel's next turn, but the angel can Sustain it indefinitely—when the carrion angel chooses to stop Sustaining it, they cannot use Living Facade again for 24 hours. The carrion angel's blasphemous stench aura is suppressed for as long as they maintain their Living Facade.

Lavinia Bavah.name: Lavinia Bavah
Lavinia Bavah.publicNotes:
The ghost commoner is an ordinary person who believes they died unjustly.

When some mortals die through tragic circumstances or without closure, their souls can linger and haunt a locale significant to them in life.

Site Bound.name: Site Bound
Site Bound.description: A typical ghost can stray only a short distance from where it was killed or the place it haunts. A typical limit is 120 feet. Some ghosts are instead bound to a room, building, item, or creature that was special to it rather than a location.

Rejuvenation.name: Rejuvenation
Rejuvenation.description:
Setting right the injustice that led to the commoner's death allows it to move on to the afterlife.

When a ghost is destroyed, it re-forms after [[/br 2d4 #days]]{2d4 days} within the location it's bound to, fully healed. A ghost can be permanently destroyed only if someone determines the reason for its existence and sets right whatever prevents the spirit from resting.

Haunted by the Night.name: Haunted by the Night
Haunted by the Night.description: After dark, Lavinia loses all reason and becomes overtaken by the curse. She loses the ability to speak and attacks the PCs on sight. While haunted by the night, Lavinia is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened}, and can use the extra action to make a ghostly hand Strike.

Infect Shame.name: Infect Shame
Infect Shame.description:
Lavinia stares at a creature she can see within 30 feet, and transfers her overwhelming shame into that creature's mind. That creature takes @Damage[3d6[mental]] damage and must attempt a @Check[will|dc:22|options:damaging-effect,inflicts:slowed] save with the following effects.

Critical Success No effect and temporarily immune for 1 minute.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage, and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 round as they agonize internally over its shame.

Critical Failure As failure, but double damage and slowed 1 for 1 minute.

Consume Flesh.name: Consume Flesh
Consume Flesh.description:
Requirements The ghoul is adjacent to the corpse of a creature that died within the last hour.

Effect The ghoul devours a chunk of the corpse and regains @Damage[5d6[healing]] Hit Points.

It can regain Hit Points from any given corpse only once.

Ghoul Whispers.name: Ghoul Whispers
Ghoul Whispers.description:
Requirements A @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} creature is within the ghoul's reach

Stage 3 as stage 2

Stage 4 as stage 2 unless the target has consumed raw meat in the past 24 hours, then it takes @Damage[4d6[void]] damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} until it consumes raw meat;

Stage 5 if the creature has eaten raw meat in the past 24 hours, it dies and rises as a ghoul, if not, it returns to stage 4

Grisly Display.name: Grisly Display
Grisly Display.description:
The ghoulrilla howls and claws at its flesh, flinging bits of matted fur, gristle, and rancid meat in a nauseating display. The ghoulrilla takes @Damage[1d6[slashing]] damage, and all creatures within @Template[type:emanation|distance:30] feet must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:23] save. While a creature is sickened by this ability, it is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} to the ghoulrilla.

Critical Success The creatures is unaffected and temporarily immune for 1 minute.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}.

Critical Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2}, and a piece of the ghoulrilla's body or rancid blood got into the creature's mouth, open wound, or otherwise infected them—the creature is exposed to forbidden cravings (see Ghoul Whispers).

Swift Leap.name: Swift Leap
Swift Leap.description: The ghoul jumps up to half its Speed. This movement doesn't trigger reactions.

Meant to Live.name: Meant to Live
Meant to Live.description: Whenever an unrisen would take damage from vitality energy, it instead heals half that number of Hit Points.

Resurrection Vulnerability.name: Resurrection Vulnerability
Resurrection Vulnerability.description: A creature with a prepared or spontaneous spell that can restore the dead to life (such as @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Hnc7eGi7vyZenAIm]{Breath of Life} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.IkGYwHRLhkuoGReG]{Raise Dead}) can expend an appropriate spell slot as a 2-action activity to destroy an unrisen within 30 feet. The attempt fails if the unrisen succeeds at a Will save against the creature's spell DC.

Rise Again.name: Rise Again
Rise Again.description:
As unrisen, but the heart-like @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.JmlPFAbjPvbhhKeu]{Vile Remnant} lodged within the creature's chest becomes momentarily visible as it's returned by this ability, allowing The Mistake to use Show the Horror.

If the unrisen is reduced to 0 Hit Points by means other than fire damage, disintegration, or its resurrection vulnerability, it returns to unlife at the start of its next turn. It has 100 Hit Points and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} in the space in which it was destroyed. The unrisen can't be returned by this ability again for 1 hour.

Agonized Howl.name: Agonized Howl
Agonized Howl.description: The unrisen howls in pain at its cursed existence. Creatures within a @Template[type:emanation|distance:30] take @Damage[10d8[mental]|options:area-damage] damage with a @Check[will|dc:32|basic] save. The unrisen can't use Agonized Howl again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Agonized Howl]]{1d4 rounds}.

Awful Approach.name: Awful Approach
Awful Approach.description:
Frequency once per 10 minutes

Effect The unrisen reshapes its grotesque form to move swiftly. It Strides twice. Any living creature that can see the unrisen during this movement must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:29] save or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} on a critical failure); this is a mental and visual effect.

Death Grip.name: Death Grip
Death Grip.description:
Requirements The unrisen has a living creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}

Effect The unrisen attempts to destroy its victim's life force so it shares in the unrisen's fate. The creature must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:32] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1}. While the curse lasts, the creature regains only half as many HP from effects with both the healing and vitality traits; if it dies, any attempt to raise it from the dead causes it to return as an unrisen. The curse ends automatically if the creature's doomed value is reduced to 0.

Show the Horror.name: Show the Horror
Show the Horror.description:
Requirements The Mistake has used rise again within the previous hour

Effect The Mistake grabs onto its chest and tugs it open, cracking ribs and tearing flesh to give a glimpse of the horrible @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.JmlPFAbjPvbhhKeu]{Vile Remnant} lodged inside of it. All creatures within 30 feet must attempt a @Check[will|dc:32|options:area-effect,inflicts:frightened,inflicts:slowed] save with the following results. The Mistake can't Show the Horror again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Show the Horror]]{1d4 rounds}.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is unsettled by the sight and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} and feels something shift in its own chest, as if a similarly shaped horror was within its own ribcage and twitching in delight at seeing its twin in another place. The affected creature can't reduce its frightened condition below 1 as long as The Mistake remains active and within 60 feet.

Critical Failure As failure, but @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3}, and the creature continues to feel that awful chest twitch any time thereafter it becomes frightened. The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} whenever it's frightened as it uses one of its actions to grip at its chest and worry about the implications of what might be inside of it; this curse has an unlimited duration.

Servitor Phantom (Cook).name: Servitor Phantom (Cook)
Servitor Phantom (Cook).allSaves: -1 status penalty to all saves vs. death effects

Bound to Bastardhall.name: Bound to Bastardhall
Bound to Bastardhall.description: Unlike the typical phantom, these phantoms exist fully in the Ethereal Plane and cannot shift back and forth between this plane and the Universe.

-1 Status to All Saves vs. Death Effects.name: -1 Status to All Saves vs. Death Effects

Skull-Faced Servant.name: Skull-Faced Servant
Skull-Faced Servant.description:
A servitor phantom's head is that of an animal skull, as determined by their original role in the castle before the curse fell. This skull head grants the servitor phantom a horns or jaws Strike (as appropriate). Each type of skull is associated with a different Lore skill.

Brewers have deer skulls and Alcohol Lore.

Cooks have bird skulls and Cooking Lore.

Housekeepers have cat skulls and Labor Lore.

Valets have dog skulls and Labor Lore.

Susceptible to Death.name: Susceptible to Death
Susceptible to Death.description:
Though phantoms aren't alive, neither are they undead, and they are uniquely vulnerable to the effects of death.

A phantom whose Hit Points are reduced to 0 as a result of a death effect (such as from a spell like @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Z9OrRXKgAPv6Hn5l]{Execute}) is immediately whisked away to the River of Souls, where their soul resumes the usual path to the afterlife.

Phantom Touch.name: Phantom Touch
Phantom Touch.description: Each time they make a Strike, a phantom can choose to deal spirit damage instead of the normal physical damage type.

Middenworm.name: Middenworm
Middenworm.publicNotes:
Creepers of sewers and crawlers within urban dump sites, middenworms are dangerous scavengers. Eager to abandon their bottom-feeding ways, they're known to attack living foes, for fresh blood is their favorite repast. A middenworm is unpleasant to look at, listen to, or smell: a greasy maggot-like worm with hooked jaws at one end that peel back the folds of its body when it bites, and a nest of long, red, blood-drinking tendrils at the other.

Giant Middenworms

Normally, a middenworm doesn’t grow much larger than a dog, as this smaller size affords them more mobility in the sewers they frequent. Yet rarely, when middenworms have more room to grow in an area that’s particularly infused with toxic magic or fiendish influences, these creatures can grow to enormous size.

Nauseating Presence.name: Nauseating Presence
Nauseating Presence.description:
30 feet. @Check[fortitude|dc:19|options:area-effect,inflicts:sickened,inflicts:slowed]

As stench, but the aura affects a creature that sees, hears, or smells the middenworm.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.Stench]

Blood Drain.name: Blood Drain
Blood Drain.description:
Requirements A @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious}, or willing creature is within reach of the middenworm's tails

Effect The middenworm drains blood from the victim, which must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:22|options:inflicts:drained] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1}. If the creature is already drained, its drained value increases by 1 (to a maximum of drained 4). The middenworm becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} until the end of its next turn, and can use the extra action to Stride, Climb, Swim, or Strike.

Midden Fever.name: Midden Fever
Midden Fever.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:22|options:inflicts:enfeebled,inflicts:fatigued,inflicts:paralyzed]

Stage 1 carrier with no ill effects (1 day)

Stage 2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} (1 day)

Stage 3 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 2} (1 day)

Stage 4 enfeebled 2 and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued} (1 day)

Stage 5 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed} (1 day)

Anophilex.name: Anophilex
Anophilex.publicNotes:
The sight of blood is frightening proof of another's suffering, and when that blood is one's own, that fear can turn to blinding terror. Such are the horrors that the skittering, constantly bleeding anophilex sahkil revels in. With a glistening, spiderlike body covered in pulsing sacs of blood caught amid tangles of thorny vines, an anophilex's head is a freshly skinned skull with sharp fangs and patches of long black hair pulled back to tangle amid the thorns of their bodies. As an anophilex moves, their thorns rip and tear at their bloody blisters and bloated organs, yet the bleeding only flows back along their body to form new thorny lengths in a constant recreation that gives off an unsettling, gurgling susurrus. An anophilex has little patience for subtlety or manipulation, preferring to skitter through or flap above battlefields, among refugees, or amid any area where the wounded gather, so they can spread fear and drink the wounded's crimson pain.

About Sahkils

Sahkils are fiends associated with primal fears and phobic terrors that haunt mortal minds. They hail from the depths of the Ethereal Plane and serve sinister demigods known collectively as tormentors, such as Charg himself. For more information about sahkils, see page 274 of Pathfinder Monster Core 2.

Easy to Call.name: Easy to Call
Easy to Call.description: An anophilex's level is considered 2 lower for the purpose of being conjured by the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.2ykmAVKrsAWcazcC]{Binding Circle} ritual (and potentially other rituals, at the GM's discretion), but it is always free to attack or leave instead of negotiate unless the primary caster's check is a critical success.

Fearful Bleeding.name: Fearful Bleeding
Fearful Bleeding.description: 30 feet. The sight and sound of the anophilex's constantly bleeding body fills non-sahkils with fears that their own blood wants to flow and surge from their veins as well. Creatures taking persistent bleed damage become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} when they enter the aura or start their turn in the aura.

Drain Blood.name: Drain Blood
Drain Blood.description: When the anophilex uses a jaws strike against a creature that's taking persistent bleed damage, they drink the blood. The creature must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:30] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 2} on a critical failure). The anophilex becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} on the following round, and can use the extra action to Stride or Strike.

Skip Between.name: Skip Between
Skip Between.description: The sahkil moves from the Universe to the Ethereal Plane or vice-versa. While in the Ethereal Plane, they're unable to affect anything in the Universe, and they cannot be seen by beings or abilities in the Universe, unless these have an ability that can gaze into the Ethereal Plane. While on the Material Plane the inverse is true for anything on the Ethereal Plane. A summoned sahkil can't use Skip Between.

Spray Vile Blood.name: Spray Vile Blood
Spray Vile Blood.description: The anophilex twists their body into a knot, causing their thorns to pierce their body so that unholy blood sprays out in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:30]. Non-sahkil creatures in this area take @Damage[12d6[spirit]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[will|dc:30|basic|options:area-effect] save). The anophilex can't Spray Vile Blood again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Spray Vile Blood]]{1d4 rounds}.

Mymnian.name: Mymnian
Mymnian.publicNotes:
A mymnian enjoys the unique fear and foolish, panic-induced acts that mortals display when confronted with what they fear to be ghosts. Be it a mymnian that uses their own abilities to mimic a haunted abode or one that settles into an area with actual ghosts, a haunted house under the watchful eye of one of these manipulative sahkils is never a safe place for the living. Typically, a mymnian wears what appears to be a billowing gray cloak to look like an oversized humanoid figure, only to cast aside the cloak to reveal that their head and torso are a mass of humanoid and animal skulls, melted into a hideous conglomeration with each bony face looking outward in different directions. They walk upon five long skeletal arms that end in bony, humanlike hands. And that cloak? Nothing less unsettling than long, rippling folds of leathery flesh that hang from their body like a cape.

Eerie Rumors

Towns that host a haunted house would expect most people to steer clear of them, but there's always a reason for someone new to brave the terrors. Rumors might spread about lost treasures, some might dare friends to "just spend one night," or others might seek to learn tantalizing secrets from the beyond; whatever the form, these lures are cultivated by a mymnian, eager to draw new victims into their playground.

Easy to Call.name: Easy to Call
Easy to Call.description: A mymnian's level is considered 2 lower for the purpose of being conjured by the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.2ykmAVKrsAWcazcC]{Binding Circle} ritual (and potentially other rituals, at the GM's discretion), but it is always free to attack or leave instead of negotiate unless the primary caster's check is a critical success.

Watchful Presence.name: Watchful Presence
Watchful Presence.description:
60 feet. Even when a mymnian doesn't notice you, you feel like they—or something worse—are watching. A creature that begins its turn inside the aura feels an overwhelming sense of being watched, gaining a +2 status bonus to Perception checks but taking a –2 penalty to saving throws against fear effects. A creature in the aura can't reduce the value of its @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened} condition below 1.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.92AQMrhyd4QmygcE]{Effect: Watchful Presence}

Doomed to Rise.name: Doomed to Rise
Doomed to Rise.description: A creature that dies from an attack by a mymnian while frightened becomes a ghost within the next 24 hours.

Extract Ghost.name: Extract Ghost
Extract Ghost.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The mymnian attempts a claw Strike. If it hits, it deals no damage—instead, the mymnian's claws hook onto the target's soul and, for a moment, tug it out of the body so that the victim can catch a glimpse of how it will look after it dies. The target takes @Damage[5d8[mental]] damage with a @Check[will|dc:33|options:damaging-effect,inflicts:frightened] save.

Critical Success The target takes no damage.

Success The target takes half damage.

Failure The target takes full damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Critical Failure The target takes double damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Wolf Empathy.name: Wolf Empathy
Wolf Empathy.description: The werecreature can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the Diplomacy skill with animals of its general kind.

Fearful of the Frost.name: Fearful of the Frost
Fearful of the Frost.description: Dazerien lost a few toes to frostbite, but what clings in his mind is the agony of the cold that seeped into his bones as he endured a particularly cruel punishment from his father. The first time each round he takes cold damage, Dazerien takes @Damage[2d6[mental]] damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} if the triggering cold damage was in excess of 20).

Abduct.name: Abduct
Abduct.description:
Requirements Dazerien has a Medium or smaller creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}

Effect Dazerien attempts to carry off his victim. The grabbed creature attempts a @Check[fortitude|dc:30] save with the following effects.

Critical Success The grabbed creature escapes and is no longer grabbed.

Success The grabbed creature remains grabbed.

Failure As success, but Dazerien can Stride, and carries the grabbed creature with him. When he's Large as a result of Moon Frenzy, Dazerien can carry up to 22 Bulk without becoming encumbered—generally more than enough to haul away a Medium (6 Bulk) creature with all their gear and armor at full speed.

Critical Failure As failure, plus Dazerien gains a +4 circumstance bonus to Athletics on his next attempt to [[/act grapple]] the grabbed creature.

Change Shape.name: Change Shape
Change Shape.description:
• Human

    • Melee fist +24 Damage 1d4+13

  • Wolf

    • Speed 40 feet

    • Knockdown

The werecreature changes into its humanoid, hybrid, or animal shape. Each shape has a specific, persistent appearance. A true werecreature's natural form is its hybrid shape.

In humanoid shape, the werecreature uses its original humanoid size, loses its jaws and claws Strikes, and gains a melee fist Strike that deals bludgeoning damage equal to the slashing damage dealt by its claw.

In animal shape, its Speed and size change to that of the animal, it gains any special Strike effects of the animal that it didn't already have (such as Grab), and it loses its weapon Strikes.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ChangeShape]

Coat Longbow.name: Coat Longbow
Coat Longbow.description:
Requirements At least one magic oil or poison is stored inside the rune's extradimensional space

Effect For 1 minute, you can apply stored oils and poisons to the weapon without needing any hands free. Applying them takes the same number of actions as normal. An oil or poison applied this way pours directly from the extradimensional space onto the weapon, and when it's fully applied, its empty vial is ejected.

Curse of the Werewolf.name: Curse of the Werewolf
Curse of the Werewolf.description:
This curse affects only humanoids.

Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:30]

On each full moon, the cursed creature must succeed at another Fortitude save or turn into the same kind of werecreature until dawn.

The creature is under the GM's control and goes on a rampage for half the night before falling unconscious until dawn.

Moon Frenzy.name: Moon Frenzy
Moon Frenzy.description:
When a full moon appears in the night sky, the werecreature must enter hybrid form, can't Change Shape thereafter, becomes one size larger, increases its reach by 5 feet, and increases the damage of its jaws by 2.

When the moon sets or the sun rises, the werecreature returns to humanoid form and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued} for [[/br 2d4 #hours]]{2d4 hours}.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.dRe8n1nBWMIXd8jh]{Effect: Moon Frenzy}

Painful Wound.name: Painful Wound
Painful Wound.description:
Trigger Dazerien deals damage with a melee Strike

Effect Dazerien tears at the victim's flesh, dealing @Damage[1d6[bleed]] and causing the victim to become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} from the pain (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} on a failed @Check[fortitude|dc:30] save).

Caydserris Arudora.name: Caydserris Arudora
Caydserris Arudora.blurb: Male fiendish human oracle of ancestors

Charg's Final Gift.name: Charg's Final Gift
Charg's Final Gift.description:
As soon as Caydserris is reduced to 0 Hit Points, he shrieks in exaltation. His head rips free from his body, which crumbles to the ground as a matrix of flesh and bone extend outward around his head, transforming him into a monstrous unique sahkil. His head and face remain, but rather than atop a humanoid body, it sits at the center of a great wheel of bone and gristle, held in place at the center by thick strings of viscera, entrails, veins, and vertebrae. Eyes and mouths open and weep along the wheel's meat-and-bristle-encrusted rim, as do five long distorted skinless arms that end in seven-fingered talons. Caydserris's wheel body floats in the air and slowly rotates, yet his head remains at all times aligned upright as the grisly spokes that connect it to the wheel constantly rip free and reattach to hold the head in place. All PCs within @Template[emanation|distance:60]{60 feet} must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:33|options:area-effect,inflicts:frightened] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} on a critical failure), and Caydserris regains @Damage[100[healing]] HP. At the same moment, Florin's soul wrenches completely free from Caydserris's dropped mace and rises up with a howl of rage to swoop back and forth through his new body.

In this new form, Caydserris's @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zXZjC8HLaRoLR17U]{Cursebound} condition increases to 2 (or increases his current cursebound condition value by 1). He loses his mace Strike but gains his fearful claw Strike. He can't cast spells in this form and loses his base Speed (but not his fly Speed). If he survives, whether or not Charg allows him to eventually return to his human form is up to you.

Florin's Revenge.name: Florin's Revenge
Florin's Revenge.description: On the start of each of Caydserris's turns, after he's gained Charg's final gift, Florin's vengeful soul deals @Damage[6d6[spirit]] damage to him (@Check[will|dc:35|basic] save).

Charg's Blessing.name: Charg's Blessing
Charg's Blessing.description:
Caydserris increases his @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zXZjC8HLaRoLR17U]{Cursebound} condition's value by 1, then targets a creature he can see within 60 feet. That creature's body distorts and partially transforms, changing limbs into monstrous appendages that are difficult to control. The target must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:36|options:inflicts:clumsy] save with the following results; regardless of the save, the target is temporarily immune to Charg's Blessing for 24 hours.

Critical Success The target recovers their body's shape immediately and is unaffected; Caydserris's cursebound condition value increases by 2 instead of 1 for using this ability.

Success The target becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} for 1 round.

Failure The target becomes clumsy 1 with an unlimited duration.

Critical Failure The target becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} with an unlimited duration.

Curse of Ancestral Meddling.name: Curse of Ancestral Meddling
Curse of Ancestral Meddling.description: When Caydserris has the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zXZjC8HLaRoLR17U]{Cursebound} condition, he becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy} with a value equal to his cursebound value as Arudora spirits—particularly that of Florin Kindler—vie for control of his mind and hinder his movements.

Terror.name: Terror
Terror.description: Caydserris can only make fearful claw Strikes once he receives Charg's Final Gift. A creature that takes damage from a fearful claw strike becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} on a critical hit).

Unholy Bloodshed.name: Unholy Bloodshed
Unholy Bloodshed.description:
Frequency once per day

Trigger Caydserris critically succeeds at an attack roll against a holy creature with his Unholy Mace

Effect The target takes @Damage[3d8[bleed]].

Whispers of Weakness.name: Whispers of Weakness
Whispers of Weakness.description: Spirits guide Caydserris. He increases his @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zXZjC8HLaRoLR17U]{Cursebound} value by 1, then targets one creature within 60 feet and gains knowledge of their weaknesses, which of their saving throw modifiers is lowest, and a +2 status bonus to his next attack roll against that foe before the end of his turn; the target is then temporarily immune for 1 day.

Ausken Dast.name: Ausken Dast
Ausken Dast.allSaves: –1 status penalty to all saves vs. death effects

Bound to Bastardhall.name: Bound to Bastardhall
Bound to Bastardhall.description: Unlike the typical phantom, Ausken exists fully in the Ethereal Plane and cannot shift back and forth between this plane and the Universe.

–1 Status Penalty to All Saves vs. Death.name: –1 Status Penalty to All Saves vs. Death

Bound Even in Death.name: Bound Even in Death
Bound Even in Death.description: As phantom, but if Ausken is reduced to 0 Hit Points by any means, his soul does not return to the River of Souls. Instead, his soul is drawn into the soul vortex in the vault under Bastardhall (area I).

Physical Manifestation.name: Physical Manifestation
Physical Manifestation.description: Upon reaching rank 1, Ausken manifests a semi-physical body. He loses the incorporeal trait, his immunities and resistances, and his fly Speed, and gains a land Speed of 25 feet. He has a Strength modifier of +5, an Athletics modifier of +12, an AC of 22, 78 HP, and can use Sheriff's Blessing. His other statistics do not change.

Phantom Touch.name: Phantom Touch
Phantom Touch.description: Each time they make a Strike, a phantom can choose to deal spirit damage instead of the normal physical damage type.

Sheriff's Blessing.name: Sheriff's Blessing
Sheriff's Blessing.description:
Requirements Ausken has a physical body

Frequency once per day

Effect Ausken touches a willing character and infuses their mind and spirit with bravery. Until the next sunset, the touched character gains a +1 status bonus to all saving throws against fear effects, and any time the character gains the frightened condition, reduce its value by 1. Ausken is always willing and eager to give his blessing to a PC when asked.

Rank 2 The blessed character now treats any success on a saving throw against a fear effect as a critical success instead.

Rank 3 Ausken can touch two willing characters to give both of them his blessing, and the effects of the blessing now last for 24 hours.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.dzBuNTGOChte8kWp]{Effect: Sheriff's Blessing}

Rhapsodic Flourish.name: Rhapsodic Flourish
Rhapsodic Flourish.description:
Trigger The Ghostlight Sister would roll a save against an auditory or sonic effect

Effect The Ghostlight Sister performs a refrain that deflects sonic vibrations and rolls a @Check[performance] check in place of the triggering saving throw. Sonic feedback rebounds from the effect, dealing @Damage[1d6[sonic]] damage to the source of the triggering effect if the Performance check succeeded or @Damage[2d6[sonic]] damage to the Ghostlight Sister on a failure.

Soloist's Curse.name: Soloist's Curse
Soloist's Curse.description:
Requirements Trio's Torment is in effect

Effect The Ghostlight Sister performs a haunting solo. This sustains an ongoing Trio's Torment if at least one other Ghostlight Sister is taking part. The Ghostlight Sister targets a single creature she can see within 60 feet as the focus of her unsettling music; that creature must attempt a @Check[will|dc:24|options:damaging-effect,inflicts:clumsy] save with the following effects. The Ghostlight Sister can't use Soloist's Curse again for 1 minute; if all Ghostlight Sisters in a Trio's Torment can't use Soloist's Curse, then the ongoing Trio's Torment ends and all three Ghostlight Sisters can't use Trio's Torment for 1 minute.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes @Damage[3d6[mental]] damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} for 1 round as the music dredges up what feel like repressed memories of forgotten agonies.

Failure As success, but @Damage[6d6[mental]] damage and clumsy 1 for 1 hour.

Critical Failure As failure, but @Damage[12d6[mental]] damage and clumsy 1 with an unlimited duration.

Trio's Torment.name: Trio's Torment
Trio's Torment.description:
The Ghostlight Sister begins playing a catchy song that compels others to dance. If other Ghostlight Sisters within 30 feet of her want to join the Trio's Torment, the Ghostlight Sister can delay to begin the torment. In this case, the effect occurs after the last Ghostlight Sister uses Trio's Torment or when one of them chooses to complete that round of the torment. Each non–Ghostlight Sister in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:50] must attempt a @Check[will|dc:24|options:inflicts:frightened] save; for each additional Ghostlight Sister involved, the save DC increases by 1 (to a maximum of DC 26). The effect lasts until the end of the next round, but if all of the Ghostlight Sisters choose to Sustain the effect on all affected creatures that remain within the emanation, the effect persists for one additional round.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune for 1 hour.

Success The creature can't use actions with the move trait except to dance, which uses the Stride action to move up to half the creature's Speed. If the creature has other Speeds, it can also dance using those modes of travel. If it's after dark, the creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure As success, and the creature must spend at least 1 action each turn dancing; the creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3}.

Servitor Phantom (Housekeeper).name: Servitor Phantom (Housekeeper)
Servitor Phantom (Housekeeper).allSaves: -1 status penalty to all saves vs. death effects

Bound to Bastardhall.name: Bound to Bastardhall
Bound to Bastardhall.description: Unlike the typical phantom, these phantoms exist fully in the Ethereal Plane and cannot shift back and forth between this plane and the Universe.

-1 Status to All Saves vs. Death Effects.name: -1 Status to All Saves vs. Death Effects

Skull-Faced Servant.name: Skull-Faced Servant
Skull-Faced Servant.description:
A servitor phantom's head is that of an animal skull, as determined by their original role in the castle before the curse fell. This skull head grants the servitor phantom a horns or jaws Strike (as appropriate). Each type of skull is associated with a different Lore skill.

Brewers have deer skulls and Alcohol Lore.

Cooks have bird skulls and Cooking Lore.

Housekeepers have cat skulls and Labor Lore.

Valets have dog skulls and Labor Lore.

Susceptible to Death.name: Susceptible to Death
Susceptible to Death.description:
Though phantoms aren't alive, neither are they undead, and they are uniquely vulnerable to the effects of death.

A phantom whose Hit Points are reduced to 0 as a result of a death effect (such as from a spell like @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Z9OrRXKgAPv6Hn5l]{Execute}) is immediately whisked away to the River of Souls, where their soul resumes the usual path to the afterlife.

Phantom Touch.name: Phantom Touch
Phantom Touch.description: Each time they make a Strike, a phantom can choose to deal spirit damage instead of the normal physical damage type.

Poisoned Skull.name: Poisoned Skull
Poisoned Skull.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:31] to identify the toxin and delicately wipe it free before burning the tainted cloth; on a critical success, the character can pinpoint two areas where the skull can be safely carried and, perhaps, used as an improvised thrown weapon to poison a creature.
Poisoned Skull.hazarddescription: A fast-acting toxin that's almost invisible to the eye coats the first and seventh skull on this display shelf.

Stain and Pain.name: Stain and Pain
Stain and Pain.description:
Trigger A creature comes in contact with the skull

Effect The contact poison turns the exposed flesh a deep scarlet color that persists for 24 hours and also afflicts the creature with nettleweed residue.

Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:27|traits:poison]

Onset 1 minute

Maximum Duration 6 minutes

Stage 1 @Damage[3d6[poison]] damage (1 minute)

Stage 2 @Damage[4d6[poison]] damage (1 minute)

Stage 3 @Damage[6d6[poison]] damage (1 minute)

Disgruntled Diners.name: Disgruntled Diners
Disgruntled Diners.disable: @Check[intimidation|dc:25] (trained) to threaten the ghostly guests into submission or @Check[religion|dc:28] (expert) to exorcise the haunt; two successes are required to disable it.
Disgruntled Diners.hazarddescription: Phantasmal diners begin hurling phantom food and very real, sharp cutlery in a dangerous food fight that targets intruders.
Disgruntled Diners.routine: (1 action) On the haunt's initiative, the phantoms hurl ghostly food and real silverware through the room. All creatures other than Ilza who are in the area take @Damage[(2d8+9)[piercing]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:24|basic|options:area-effect] save) from the sharp forks and knives being thrown about.
Disgruntled Diners.reset: The haunt deactivates at the start of any round in which Ilza is the only other creature present, then immediately resets.

Any Excuse for a Food Fight.name: Any Excuse for a Food Fight
Any Excuse for a Food Fight.description:
Trigger Ilza attacks the PCs

Effect Upon seeing Ilza's anger, the guests rise up in a flurry of activity, their voices suddenly loud and startling. Every PC in area D6 must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:24|options:area-effect,inflicts:off-guard] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} for the first round of combat. The haunt then rolls initiative.

Vinlach.name: Vinlach
Vinlach.publicNotes:
The vinlach represents the overwhelming fear of birds—the sharp beaks, the razored talons, the incessantly fluttering wings, the alien all-seeing eyes, and the haunting shrill cry of the raptor when it spots defenseless prey. They appear as a tangled mass of flapping whippoorwill wings, constantly kicking up dander and dust, with a "head" composed of dozens of shrieking whippoorwill heads, all merged together in a twittering knot of meat and bone, eyes peering in all directions at once. The amalgamation stalks about on four long, stork-like legs tipped with murderous talons, and while their body of wings wouldn't seem to suggest it, they can use them to fly through the air with unnerving grace. Despite their bestial nature, vinlachs are quite intelligent and delight in tormenting sapient creatures, particularly those who have strong beliefs or faiths.

Psychopomp Blasphemers

While all sahkils descended from an initial group of blasphemous psychopomps who betrayed their calling and rebelled against Pharasma, the eerie vinlachs take this corruption one step further in their desecration of Pharasma's sacred animal—the whippoorwill. They take particular delight in haunting fallen churches of Pharasma or serving priests who have turned their back on the Lady of Graves for more sinister patrons.

Easy to Call.name: Easy to Call
Easy to Call.description: A vinlach's level is considered 2 lower for the purpose of being conjured by the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.2ykmAVKrsAWcazcC]{Binding Circle} ritual (and potentially other rituals, at the GM's discretion), but it is always free to attack or leave instead of negotiate unless the primary caster's check is a critical success.

Soul-Wrenching Warbling.name: Soul-Wrenching Warbling
Soul-Wrenching Warbling.description:
The vinlach's warbling voices are a mockery of the rhythmic sound of a flight of whippoorwills whistling away, sending chills into the hearts of those who hear them. A living creature that begins its turn within 30 feet of a vinlach must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:23|options:area-effect] save or gain weakness 5 to spirit damage until the start of its next turn, as its soul aches to flee its body and retreat along the River of Souls to find peace from the unnerving cacophony.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.rIyN5x93mvV28dC1]{Effect: Soul-Wrenching Warbling}

Skip Between.name: Skip Between
Skip Between.description: The sahkil moves from the Universe to the Ethereal Plane or vice-versa. While in the Ethereal Plane, they're unable to affect anything in the Universe, and they cannot be seen by beings or abilities in the Universe, unless these have an ability that can gaze into the Ethereal Plane. While on the Material Plane the inverse is true for anything on the Ethereal Plane. A summoned sahkil can't use Skip Between.

Soul Shriek.name: Soul Shriek
Soul Shriek.description:
The vinlach's dozens of mouths suddenly shriek in terrifying unison, yet the sound created is not one that can be heard by ears—rather, it's heard by a living creature's soul, as the supernatural sound attempts to rip free the very animus of life. All creatures in a @Template[type:cone|distance:40] take @Damage[9d6[spirit]|options:area-damage] damage and must attempt a @Check[will|dc:26] save with the following results. The vinlach can't Soul Shriek again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Soul Shriek]]{1d4 rounds}.

Critical Success The creature takes no damage.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage. If the creature can cast divine spells or has the holy trait, it's also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage. If the creature can cast divine spells or has the holy trait, it's also stupefied 1 for 24 hours.

Blasphemous Blood.name: Blasphemous Blood
Blasphemous Blood.disable: @Check[religion|dc:23] to exorcise the influence of Charg from a statue, @Check[thievery|dc:26] to dismantle the magical blood generator in a statue's neck, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (3rd-rank, counteract DC 20) to render a statue inert; each statue must be disabled separately
Blasphemous Blood.hazarddescription: The walls and ceiling begin bleeding more and more, and gouts of cursed blood spew from both decapitated statues' necks.
Blasphemous Blood.routine:
(2 actions) The hazard sprays a sizzling gout of cursed blood from the neck stumps of each of the defiled statues of Pharasma for each of its actions. If a statue is disabled or destroyed, the hazard loses that corresponding action. Each gout targets a randomly determined non-sahkil creature in area C13, who must then attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:22] save against the following effects. After dark, this trap gains 4 actions instead of 2, with each statue firing two gouts of blood. Regardless of how many gouts are fired, a creature can be targeted only once per round by these gouts.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes @Damage[2d6[spirit]] damage.

Failure The target takes @Damage[2d8[spirit]] damage, @Damage[1d6[persistent,bleed]] damage, and is exposed to the curse of death's blood.

Critical Failure The target takes @Damage[4d8[spirit]] damage, @Damage[2d6[persistent,bleed]] damage, and is exposed to the curse of death's blood (and takes a –2 circumstance penalty to save against the curse).
Blasphemous Blood.reset: The blasphemous blood deactivates at the start of any round in which no creatures other than a sahkil are in area C13, then resets after 3 rounds.

Let the Walls Weep Blood.name: Let the Walls Weep Blood
Let the Walls Weep Blood.description:
Trigger A non-sahkil creature moves more than 10 feet into area C13

Effect The walls and ceiling begin to weep blood at an alarming rate, causing the floor of area C13 to grow slick. A non-sahkil that moves across the slick floor is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} and must [[/act balance]] (@Check[acrobatics|dc:20]) as long as the hazard remains active. An area of effect with the cold trait created in this area freezes the blood on the floor, making it even more slippery (increasing the Acrobatics check to Balance to DC 22). The hazard then rolls initiative.

Curse of Death's Blood.name: Curse of Death's Blood
Curse of Death's Blood.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:22]

Effect Your blood grows cold and imbued with death. Whenever you are struck by a critical hit, you take an additional @Damage[1d6[persistent,bleed]] damage, and as long as you are taking persistent bleed damage, you become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} as your body weakens under the lure of death's embrace. If you make your daily preparations at a location sanctified to Pharasma or Shelyn (such as area A9 after Shirail's phantom returns), you can attempt a new saving throw to end this curse.

Grindylow Stalker.name: Grindylow Stalker
Grindylow Stalker.publicNotes:
The top half of a grindylow vaguely resembles a goblin, but from the waist down, their bodies split into a tangle of suckered, wriggling tentacles. Grindylows mostly dwell in shallow waters, fresh and briny, including lakes, rivers, coastal regions, and coral reefs. They generally organize into groups called schools, which can range from a few individuals to a few hundred. Smaller schools are sometimes taken over by a powerful aquatic creature, though such alliances only last until the school faces a major setback, at which point the surviving grindylows scatter and form smaller schools of their own.

Grindylows aren't territorial, but they are pragmatic. While they rarely build permanent structures, they will adopt a good hunting ground for generations until driven away by predators. They often lair in mobile shelters, such as a sargasso of seaweed or hull of an abandoned ship. They are skilled scavengers and hunters who eat anything they can sink their teeth into.

Grindylows respect the power of larger sea predators but have a special hatred for squids (or anything that resembles a squid). Sailors plying grindylow-infested waters often paint the images of squids on the bottoms of their hulls in hopes of warding off potentials raids. While this can keep smaller schools at bay, it can also backfire, potentially inciting larger groups to gather for a coordinated attack; this becomes especially likely if the ship's route is predictable. Their hatred of squids does not extend to other tentacled creatures; grindylows consider octopuses to be the epitome of grace and power.

Reactive Strike (Special).name: Reactive Strike (Special)
Reactive Strike (Special).description:
A grindylow gains 1 extra reaction at the start of each of their turns that they can use only to make a Reactive Strike with a tentacle. They can't use more than one Reactive Strike triggered by the same action or choice.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ReactiveStrike]

Clinging Suckers.name: Clinging Suckers
Clinging Suckers.description:
When a grindylow successfully @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.Tkd8sH4pwFIPzqTr]{Grabs} a creature larger than themself, they attach to that creature. The @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} creature is not @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized}, but if it moves, the grindylow moves with it.

If the creature is Medium or smaller, it takes a –5-foot status penalty to its Speeds while the grindylow is attached. The grindylow is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} while attached to a creature.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.FQX3YY3iFTtAtw1k]{Effect: Clinging Suckers}

Jet.name: Jet
Jet.description: The grindylow moves up to 60 feet in a straight line through the water without triggering reactions.

Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
Sneak Attack.description: A grindylow stalker deals 1d4 extra precision damage to creatures who are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard}.

Collapsing Lift.name: Collapsing Lift
Collapsing Lift.disable: @Check[crafting|dc:32] (expert) or @Check[thievery|dc:35] (expert) to reinforce one of the anchor points; at least three of the four dangerous anchor points must be disabled to make the lift safe
Collapsing Lift.hazarddescription: The anchor points in the platform's corners suddenly tear loose, causing the entire platform to collapse into the shaft below.

Collapsing Platform.name: Collapsing Platform
Collapsing Platform.description:
Trigger The lift is raised or lowered while at least one Small or larger creature stands on it

Effect Attempt a @Check[flat|dc:11]. This DC increases by 1 for each creature on the lift that's Medium, or by 4 for each Large creature. On a success, the lift operates normally that round, but on a failure, the anchor points give way, dropping the platform and all creatures on the lift into the shaft. A falling creature can arrest their fall by Grabbing an Edge to grab one of the swinging ropes (@Check[reflex|dc:33]), otherwise the creature takes normal falling damage plus an additional @Damage[4d6[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:33|basic]) from falling debris.

Zaurgaulus.name: Zaurgaulus
Zaurgaulus.publicNotes: Fear is one of the most powerful emotions, and despair dragons are masters of channeling those feelings of terror and hopelessness for their own benefit. As with other occult dragons, despair dragons are driven by an innate compulsion, in their case, the desire to strike terror in others. Despair dragons tend to settle near settlements, so they have a source of fear to draw from. The most common items in despair dragon hoards are scrolls, tomes, and relics that serve as research material. Through these, despair dragons learn of local folklore, urban legends, and more to better haunt their targets.
Zaurgaulus.allSaves: +2 status to all saves vs. occult

Fearsense.name: Fearsense
Fearsense.description: The dragon senses all creatures with the frightened condition at the listed range.

+2 Status to All Saves vs. Occult.name: +2 Status to All Saves vs. Occult

Consume Fear.name: Consume Fear
Consume Fear.description:
Trigger A creature within 60 feet loses the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened} condition

Effect The dragon feasts upon the fear that leaves the triggering creature's body, gaining 6d8 temporary Hit Points that last for 1 minute.

Unbidden Thoughts.name: Unbidden Thoughts
Unbidden Thoughts.description:
Trigger The dragon is critically hit with a weapon or unarmed attack

Effect The attacker's mind fills with visions of their worst fears that overwhelm their senses, and they must choose one of the following results: either the triggering attack becomes a normal success, or the critical hit is unaffected but the triggering creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Draconic Frenzy.name: Draconic Frenzy
Draconic Frenzy.description: The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one tail Strike in any order.

Draconic Momentum.name: Draconic Momentum
Draconic Momentum.description: The dragon recharges their Shrieking Breath whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike.

Shrieking Breath.name: Shrieking Breath
Shrieking Breath.description: The dragon lets out a cacophonous sound made of every scream the dragon has drawn from a terrified enemy, dealing @Damage[15d6[sonic]|options:area-damage] damage in a @Template[type:cone|distance:40] (@Check[will|dc:37|basic|options:area-effect] save). Creatures who fail their Will save must spend the first action of their next turn doing nothing but screaming. The dragon can't use Shrieking Breath again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Shrieking Breath]]{1d4 rounds}.

Tongue Decoy.name: Tongue Decoy
Tongue Decoy.description:
The despair dragon inflates several bladders at the end of its tongue to create the basic form of a creature. This process takes 1 minute to complete, during which the dragon is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard}. If the dragon stops or is interrupted in this process, the bladders deflate, and the dragon must start over. Once the process is complete, the dragon can maintain the inflated bladders indefinitely, and can Dismiss to deflate the bladders and retract its tongue instantly.

The inflated tongue takes the basic form of an animal or humanoid and can be inflated to be either Small or Medium. The form resembles the general silhouette of a creature, though closer inspection and success at a @Check[perception|dc:33] check can determine the true nature of the tongue. While inflated, the dragon can send its voice through the decoy, though keeping its tongue inflated makes it difficult to speak, causing the dragon to take a –4 circumstance penalty to any checks related to speaking, such as Deception checks to Lie.

The dragon's tongue can extend up to 90 feet from the dragon's body and it can fully extend its tongue as part of the process to inflate the bladders. The dragon can move the inflated part of its tongue up to 15 feet at a time with an action, which has the concentrate, manipulate, and move traits. While extended, the inflated end of the tongue occupies space as a creature of the appropriate size, but the rest of the tongue doesn't impede or block movement in any way. The dragon's scent functions through cilia at the end of the tongue, but otherwise the dragon has no means of knowing what's near its tongue.

Attacking the tongue is the same as attacking the dragon, except that the tongue is always @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard}. If the tongue takes any damage, it immediately deflates and remains out. The dragon remains off-guard as long as its tongue is out, but the dragon can retract its tongue with two consecutive Interact actions. If the tongue takes damage, the dragon can't use its tongue decoy again for 1 day.

The noxious needlers' ability to follow orders is granted by the otherwise mindless humanoid brain that floats in their dome-like heads, allowing them to serve as laborers and guards for their creators.

In exceptionally rare cases, the brain used in their creation might retain fragments of memories or even an actual intellect, resulting in a noxious needler with a personality and agenda of its own. Unwilling creations often hunt down their creators, venting their rage on similar targets if revenge is impossible. Others blankly replicate the experiments from their last memory

The haunt uses its first three actions to target a random creature within the schoolhouse with a burning debris ranged Strike. A creature can't be targeted more than once per round—if there aren't enough targets for all 3 Strikes, the leftover Strike actions are wasted. On its fourth action, the haunt causes the fires in the building itself to flare up—all creatures inside the building take @Damage[2d8[fire]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:21|basic] save). These flare-ups are the most extreme in area A4a; creatures in areas A4b or A4c gain a +2 circumstance bonus on this Reflex save.

The Sky Breathes Smoke.description:

Effect Harrowing shrieks and frightening howls echo from the skies above as smoke plumes down into the rooms below. All creatures in the schoolhouse (areas A4a–A4c) must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:21|options:area-effect,inflicts:sickened] save to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} from the smoke (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} on a critical failure). The haunt then rolls initiative.

Phantom Knight (Bastion of Blasphemies).name: Phantom Knight (Bastion of Blasphemies)
Phantom Knight (Bastion of Blasphemies).publicNotes:
Cavaliers and knights who died for their cause make for particularly strongwilled phantoms. Though their motives vary, these phantoms often seek to continue their lifelong missions even in their purgatorial states, and their strong forces of will make them formidable fighters in spite of their incorporeality. A phantom knight might strive to find living followers of their church or order, or seek out other mortals they knew in life as a way of staying grounded and avoiding the corruption of undeath.

The typical trajectory for souls passing to the afterlife is fairly straightforward, according to most theologians. When a mortal dies, their soul enters the River of Souls and eventually reaches the Boneyard, where it is judged by Pharasma. The judged soul moves onto its appropriate domain of final rest—Heaven, Hell, Abaddon, and so forth—where it becomes a shade.

Complications arise, however, when a soul in queue for judgment prematurely departs from the River of Souls and is shunted into the Ethereal Plane. Whether as a result of nefarious interlopers like daemons or hags, malignant planar magic, or even fate, these souls become dislodged from the natural order of life and death and linger in a sort of purgatory. Unlike petitioners, these ethereal phantoms retain memories of their life before death, and unlike spirits such as ghosts, phantoms aren't tinged with the foul influences of undeath—at least, not at first, though the threat of corruption hangs heavy over a phantom's existence. Some eventually succumb to that fate, while others eventually rejoin the River of Souls. Until then, these wandering souls are a kind unto themselves—one without a true home, agenda, or purpose.

Many phantoms have no desire to remain in their strange state of purgatory, either because they seek to continue their journey through the River of Souls or because they fear the corruption of undeath. In order to complete the natural spiritual cycle and become judged so they can continue to the afterlife, a phantom must find a way back into the River of Souls. Such a quest is no easy feat, however—the hazy mists of the Ethereal Plane can befuddle even the most experienced traveler, and numerous predators prowl the realm in search of stray souls to bind or devour.
Phantom Knight (Bastion of Blasphemies).allSaves: -1 status to all saves vs. death effects

Bound to Bastardhall.name: Bound to Bastardhall
Bound to Bastardhall.description: Unlike the typical phantom, these phantoms exist fully in the Ethereal Plane and cannot shift back and forth between this plane and the Universe.

Susceptible to Death.name: Susceptible to Death
Susceptible to Death.description:
Though phantoms aren't alive, neither are they undead, and they are uniquely vulnerable to the effects of death.

A phantom whose Hit Points are reduced to 0 as a result of a death effect (such as from a spell like @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Z9OrRXKgAPv6Hn5l]{Execute}) is immediately whisked away to the River of Souls, where their soul resumes the usual path to the afterlife.

Phantom Touch.name: Phantom Touch
Phantom Touch.description: Each time they make a Strike, a phantom can choose to deal spirit damage instead of the normal physical damage type.

Agonizing Thorns.name: Agonizing Thorns
Agonizing Thorns.disable: @Check[survival|dc:27] to delicately unthread the vines from the skeleton without triggering them; four successes are required to disable the haunt.
Agonizing Thorns.hazarddescription: A massive tangle of brambles weaves through a skeleton clad in armor.

The Thorns Need Blood.name: The Thorns Need Blood
The Thorns Need Blood.description:
Trigger A person attempts to damage the vines or to Interact with the skeleton or its armor

Effect The thorny vines suddenly animate, and in so doing, make it appear that the skeleton is rising to attack. The vines lash out, and all creatures in area B2b or within 20 feet above take @Damage[8d6[slashing]] damage from the thorns (@Check[reflex|dc:29|basic] save). A creature that fails the save also takes @Damage[1d6[persistent,bleed]] damage (@Damage[2d6[persistent,bleed]] damage on a critical failure).

Nulferion.name: Nulferion
Nulferion.publicNotes: Horses serve as mounts and beasts of burden in many societies. They are loyal and typically gentle creatures, and they are invaluable to those looking to travel long distances. Smaller folk, like gnomes and halflings, often utilize ponies as mounts, while horses are the favored steeds for humans and other Medium humanoids. Most horses that the average humanoid encounters are domesticated, though large herds can be found in the wild.

Gallop.name: Gallop
Gallop.description: The war horse Strides twice. It has a +10-foot circumstance bonus to its Speed during these Strides.

Bastardhall Rat.name: Bastardhall Rat
Bastardhall Rat.publicNotes:
Giant rats are enormous versions of the common vermin. They are typically found in abundant numbers, but since they cannot fit in the nooks where mundane rats typically hide, they are much easier to locate and exterminate. They mostly live in sewers where they can scavenge from the streets above, but some families of giant rats live in more remote locations, such as dank caves, forests or hills. Rats are incredibly adept survivors and can be found nearly anywhere in the world, though they tend to favor temperate or warm climates as opposed to cold regions.

Although its bite alone is not lethal except to the very young or very old, the giant rat carries the putrid plague common to rodents around the world—a pestilence more than capable of ravaging rural communities.

Rats are a ubiquitous menace, scurrying through the sewers and on the streets of nearly every settlement in the world. Though a regular rat darting underfoot might startle or even frighten the average passerby, giant rats and rat swarms are far more dangerous.

Ratpox.name: Ratpox
Ratpox.description:
A creature that takes damage from a Bastardhall rat's bite is exposed to a painful and debilitating curse, and must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:22] save against the following effects.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected by the curse.

Success Pain shoots through the creature as angry redringed blisters form in the vicinity of the bite. The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} by the pain.

Failure As success, but @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2}. In addition, the blisters linger even after the initial pain abates, leaving the creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} from the discomfort for as long as the curse persists. Each time the sun rises, the creature can attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:22] save to end the curse's effects.

Critical Failure As failure, but the curse has an unlimited duration, and its effects grow more discomforting after dark, increasing to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 2} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} while the sun is down.

They Grow Inside.name: They Grow Inside
They Grow Inside.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:23] (expert) to reinforce the bin so it doesn't collapse (although if the PCs then search the remains, they still trigger the hazard), @Check[religion|dc:27] (master) to exorcise the haunt.
They Grow Inside.hazarddescription: When the bin is opened, it collapses, spilling out the infested corpse within.

Horrific Infestation.name: Horrific Infestation
Horrific Infestation.description:
Trigger The seed bin is opened, or the body within is jostled or searched

Effect The body spills out and splits open, releasing an agonizing scream. All creatures in area C4 must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:29] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} as long as they remain frightened on a critical failure). The ghoulish gardeners in area C7 come to investigate soon thereafter. The creature who triggered the haunt must also succeed at a @Check[will|dc:29] save with the following effects as it takes a blast of spore-like seeds to the face.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected by the infestation.

Success The creature believes it inhaled some of the stuff, and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2}.

Failure As success, but the creature now fears that it's infected by the corrupt seeds, and imagines it can feel plants growing inside itself. This is all in the creature's mind, but for the next 8 hours, the sensation makes it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2}.

Critical Failure As failure, but the clumsy condition has an unlimited duration.

Assume Form.description: The ugothol spends 10 minutes reshaping its appearance to take on the shape of any Small or Medium humanoid. It gains a +4 circumstance bonus to Deception checks to pass as that creature.

Blood Nourishment.name: Blood Nourishment
Blood Nourishment.description: The ugothol uses its three-pronged tongue to drink the blood of an adjacent @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} creature. Revert Form.description:

Effect The ugothol resumes its true form. Until the start of its next turn, it gains a +2 status bonus to attack rolls, damage rolls, saving throws, and skill checks.

Bound Even in Death.description: As phantom, but if Banijer is reduced to 0 Hit Points by any means, his soul does not return to the River of Souls. Instead, his soul is drawn into the soul vortex in the vault under Bastardhall (area I).

Physical Manifestation.name: Physical Manifestation
Physical Manifestation.description: Upon reaching rank 1, Banijer manifests a semi-physical body. He loses the incorporeal trait, his immunities and resistances, and his fly Speed, and gains a land Speed of 25 feet. He has a Strength modifier of +1, an Athletics modifier of +9, an AC of 21, 73 HP, and primal innate spells. His other statistics do not change.

Phantom Touch.description: Each time they make a Strike, a phantom can choose to deal spirit damage instead of the normal physical damage type.
