Spellcasting.description:
Once Banijer is rank 1 and has a physical body, he gains the following primal innate spells. As his rank increases, his primal spell DC and spell attack modifier increase, and he gains additional innate spells.

Primal Innate Spells DC 22, attack +14; 3rd @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.SUKaxVZW2TlM8lu0]{Cleanse Affliction}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.rfZpqmj0AIIdkVIs]{Heal}; 2nd @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.SUKaxVZW2TlM8lu0]{Cleanse Affliction}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.rfZpqmj0AIIdkVIs]{Heal}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.BCuHKrDeJ4eq53M6]{Sure Footing}; 1st @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.qXTB7Ec9yYh5JPPV]{Cleanse Cuisine}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.rfZpqmj0AIIdkVIs]{Heal}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.dINQzhqGmIsqGMUY]{Mending}; Cantrips (3rd) @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.thAHF1zxNplLCJPO]{Caustic Blast}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.gpzpAAAJ1Lza2JVl]{Detect Magic}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.WBmvzNDfpwka3qT4]{Light}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.OhD2Z6rIGGD5ocZA]{Read Aura}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.uZK2BYzPnxUBnDjr]{Tangle Vine}

Rank 2 DC 24, attack +16; 4th @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.SUKaxVZW2TlM8lu0]{Cleanse Affliction}; 3rd @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.MZGkMsPBztFN0pUO]{Water Breathing}.

His cantrips are heightened to 4th rank.

Rank 3 DC 26, attack +18; 5th @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.BCuHKrDeJ4eq53M6]{Sure Footing}; 4th @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.rfZpqmj0AIIdkVIs]{Heal}.

His cantrips are heightened to 5th rank.

Soul Glutton.name: Soul Glutton
Soul Glutton.publicNotes:
In the mist-choked fens and smoke-clogged ruins of Abaddon dwell creatures made of solid vapor whose roiling bodies drift among the fogs and effluvia of that wasted realm. Among the most unsettling of those are soul gluttons: drifting, ravenous monstrosities whose bodies shift and pulse like mist, yet are clammy and all too solid to the touch. While a soul glutton's favored meal is (naturally) souls, they eagerly attack the living to feed upon their life essence, gulping down the souls as they perish.

Soul gluttons are particularly delighted to be drawn to worlds within the Universe, for here the souls are of a much wider variety of flavors than the twisted, tormented shades that populate Abaddon. A soul glutton's eagerness to feed on worldly souls makes them notoriously difficult to control when conjured—but a promise to let them free upon the world after performing a relatively small service is often enough to secure their fleeting loyalty to a short-lived cause.

Eaters of Souls

These creatures have an unnerving affectation—they enjoy knowing those they feed upon, and before consuming a soul will often take time to converse with it while it still lives, or via talking corpse if the creature is already dead. Conversations with healthy creatures hold very little interest to soul gluttons, as life tends to distort the truths they enjoy hearing about. To a soul glutton, the greatest truths can be learned by reading the mind of a creature at the moment it passes away.

Soul Gorge.name: Soul Gorge
Soul Gorge.description: The soul glutton casts mind reading on a dying creature (or the corpse of a creature that died no more than 24 hours ago). If a dying creature fails its save, it must immediately attempt a recovery check. If the creature dies as a result of this check (or if the target was a fresh corpse), the soul glutton consumes a significant portion of the creature's soul and restores @Damage[30[healing]] Hit Points, gaining any Hit Points in excess of its maximum as temporary Hit Points that last for 24 hours. A creature slain in this way can be returned to life normally once the soul glutton that killed it has been slain, otherwise any attempt to restore life requires a @Check[flat|dc:15] for success.

Soulscar.name: Soulscar
Soulscar.description: The soul glutton's claw Strikes affect incorporeal creatures with the effects of a ghost touch property rune and scar the soul. The first time in a round that a creature is damaged by a soul glutton's claw Strike, it must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:30|options:inflicts:frightened,inflicts:doomed] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} (plus @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1} on a critical failure).

Bully the Bully.name: Bully the Bully
Bully the Bully.description:
Augsten's sense of strength and self-worth shatters whenever someone calls him "Little Lord Augie." A PC can attempt to send Augsten into a tantrum by calling him by this insult as part of a special attempt to [[/act create-a-diversion dc=24 traits=auditory,linguistic]] that has the auditory and linguistic traits, with the following results.

Critical Success Augsten is cut deep by your teasing! He becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} by his rage, and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} to your attacks for the next 24 hours. During this time, he takes a –4 circumstance penalty to all attempts to use [[/act demoralize]] on any target, and can't use Bullying Command.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.WoU5RKBuin0DOmcT]{Effect: Bully the Bully (Critical Success)}

Success Your insult enrages Augsten, causing him to become off-guard to your attacks until the start of his next turn as he's distracted by his anger. The next attempt to insult him using this by any PC gains a +2 circumstance bonus to the Deception check.

Failure Your attempt fails to rile Augsten up, but it does attract his attention. He focuses his attacks on you on his next turn.

Critical Failure Your attempt to tease Augsten backfires, and instead of sending him into a sputtering tantrum, you enrage him. He gains a +2 status bonus to all damage rolls against you for the next 24 hours, during which time you cannot attempt to Bully the Bully. Augsten favors you as his target for all attacks during this time.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.QpJ9P61zME3DYDsV]{Effect: Bully the Bully (Critical Failure)}

Reactive Bullying.name: Reactive Bullying
Reactive Bullying.description:
Trigger A creature Augsten can see fails an attack roll or skill check

Effect Augsten attempts to [[/act demoralize]] the triggering creature by taunting it with cruel laughter and insults about its ability.

Bullying Command.name: Bullying Command
Bullying Command.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect Augsten bellows out an insulting, bullying order to a bugbear tormentor he can see. That bugbear tormentor becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} until the end of their next turn, and can use the extra action to Interact, Step, Stride, or Strike.

Cruel Lashes.name: Cruel Lashes
Cruel Lashes.description: When Augsten wields a whip, the whip loses its nonlethal trait. He deals an additional 1d6 precision damage with a whip against frightened foes.

Cudgeling Blow.name: Cudgeling Blow
Cudgeling Blow.description:
Requirements Augsten is carrying his cudgel in one hand

Frequency once per round

Effect Augsten smashes his cudgel against an adjacent creature with astonishing force, dealing @Damage[3d8[bludgeoning]] damage and forcing the target to attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:26] save.

Critical Success The creature takes no damage.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} until the start of its next turn.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage, is knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}, and is off-guard until the start of its next turn.

Site Bound.name: Site Bound
Site Bound.description: These three ghosts can only leave the crypts when Bastardhall appears on Golarion, and even then, they can't leave the island.

Rejuvenation.name: Rejuvenation
Rejuvenation.description: The three adventurers re-form after [[/gmr 2d4 #days]]{2d4 days} here in the crypts unless someone carries their respective urn of ashes down to the temple in Maiserene (area A9) to be cleansed by Shirail.

Lerrisu's Dirge.name: Lerrisu's Dirge
Lerrisu's Dirge.description:
Lerrisu begins to sing a mournful dirge that unsettles the living but bolsters her ghostly allies. Each living creature within 30 feet must attempt a @Check[will|dc:28] save with the following results, while each of her ghostly companions within 30 feet become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} until the start of Lerrisu's next turn; they can use the extra action only to Fly or Strike.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} by sadness invoked by the dirge until the start of Lerrisu's next turn.

Failure As success, but also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} by sadness.

Critical Failure As failure, but @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 2}.

Malevolent Possession.name: Malevolent Possession
Malevolent Possession.description: The ghost attempts to possess an adjacent corporeal creature. This has the same effect as the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.wU6hNzK8Yfqdmc8m]{Possession} spell (@Check[will|dc:23]), except since the ghost doesn't have a physical body, it is unaffected by that restriction of the spell.

Servitor Phantom (Valet).name: Servitor Phantom (Valet)
Servitor Phantom (Valet).allSaves: -1 status penalty to all saves vs. death effects

Bound to Bastardhall.name: Bound to Bastardhall
Bound to Bastardhall.description: Unlike the typical phantom, these phantoms exist fully in the Ethereal Plane and cannot shift back and forth between this plane and the Universe.

-1 Status to All Saves vs. Death Effects.name: -1 Status to All Saves vs. Death Effects

Skull-Faced Servant.name: Skull-Faced Servant
Skull-Faced Servant.description:
A servitor phantom's head is that of an animal skull, as determined by their original role in the castle before the curse fell. This skull head grants the servitor phantom a horns or jaws Strike (as appropriate). Each type of skull is associated with a different Lore skill.

Brewers have deer skulls and Alcohol Lore.

Cooks have bird skulls and Cooking Lore.

Housekeepers have cat skulls and Labor Lore.

Valets have dog skulls and Labor Lore.

Susceptible to Death.name: Susceptible to Death
Susceptible to Death.description:
Though phantoms aren't alive, neither are they undead, and they are uniquely vulnerable to the effects of death.

A phantom whose Hit Points are reduced to 0 as a result of a death effect (such as from a spell like @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Z9OrRXKgAPv6Hn5l]{Execute}) is immediately whisked away to the River of Souls, where their soul resumes the usual path to the afterlife.

Phantom Touch.name: Phantom Touch
Phantom Touch.description: Each time they make a Strike, a phantom can choose to deal spirit damage instead of the normal physical damage type.

Rembles Worthy.name: Rembles Worthy
Rembles Worthy.publicNotes:
Barghests are canine beasts that take great joy in the hunt, often lurking near humanoid settlements to find prey that can provide a suitable challenge. Even in the deepest wilderness, barghests choose the most clever or difficult prey, searching endlessly for challenges like giants, nymphs, and unicorns.

More than victory or even the possibility of a meal at the end, barghests enjoy the thrill of the chase and the fear they create within their prey. Particularly terrified targets of a hunting barghest might even be allowed to escape, spreading the terror and enticing hunters who can become the barghest's next victims. A handful of barghests resort to learning magical methods of causing fear directly, though they find such fear hollow and unsatisfying.

Although they rarely tolerate the competition of another barghest's presence, these hunters will happily work with anyone who helps them find prey to torment and kill. This often involves enforcing the will of hags or particularly cruel fey, but a bored barghest might also force a family of weaker humanoids to work as scouts and bait.

Typical barghests often make use of their shapechanging abilities to hide in plain sight, only taking their true forms to frighten their prey and exult in the hunt. However, they are often still exposed by their trail of victims or the curiously unhealing wounds they inflict, even in humanoid form. Tales of powerful barghests with invisible heads are sometimes told in remote and dwindling villages. These barghests generally dispense with hiding as a humanoid or dog, instead terrifying entire communities and openly hunting increasingly dangerous prey. Some also extend this pride to their intellect, insisting on matching wits with their prey or even with those who believe they're hunting the barghest.

Primal Hunt.name: Primal Hunt
Primal Hunt.description:
Trigger A creature within the barghest's reach takes a move or teleportation action

Effect After the triggering action, the barghest can teleport up to 60 feet to a space adjacent to that creature.

Change Shape.name: Change Shape
Change Shape.description:
The barghest takes on the shape of a humanoid, a dog, or its true form. Their size changes to match the new form. When the barghest is a humanoid, their claw Strike deals bludgeoning damage and they lose their jaws Strike. When the barghest is a dog, their Speed changes to 35 feet. Each individual barghest has only one humanoid form and one dog form.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ChangeShape]

Isolating Howl.name: Isolating Howl
Isolating Howl.description:
Rembles lets loose an unearthly howl filled with utter despair. All creatures other than barghests within a 60 foot emanation who hear the howl become filled with the sense that they're all alone in the world, and that an impossible distance spans between themselves and anything remotely connected to companionship. Affected creatures must attempt a @Check[will|dc:24] save with the following effects.

Rembles can't use Isolating Howl again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Isolating Howl]]{1d4 rounds}.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success Convictions of loneliness fill the target's mind, and they cannot target allies or take the Aid action for 1 round.

Failure As success, but the weight of being so alone crushes down on the creature, causing them to become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 minute as well.

Critical Failure There's no reason to try. The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed} from ennui and despair for 1 minute, but can attempt a @Check[will|dc:24] save at the end of each of their turns to break free from this despair—on a success, they're no longer paralyzed but become slowed 1 for 1 minute.

Unhealing Wound.name: Unhealing Wound
Unhealing Wound.description: A creature damaged by the barghest's claws must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:24] save or be cursed. The cursed creature can't regain Hit Points except via magic until it returns to maximum Hit Points. The creature can attempt a new saving throw against the curse every 24 hours.

Infiltration Tools.name: Infiltration Tools
Infiltration Tools.description: A dig-widget's face consists of a set of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.6nrCxNQFycUVFOV2]{Infiltrator Thieves' Tools}. They can be salvaged from a destroyed dig-widget with a successful @Check[crafting|dc:20|name:Salvage Infiltration Tools] check. On a failed check, the tools are destroyed.

Mechanical Vulnerability.name: Mechanical Vulnerability
Mechanical Vulnerability.description: A creature with expert proficiency in Thievery can attempt a check to [[/act disable-device dc=20]] to damage a dig-widget. The DC is 20, and each success deals @Damage[18[untyped]] damage.

Fastening Leap.name: Fastening Leap
Fastening Leap.description: The dig-widget Leaps up 20 feet onto a creature or object and attempts a corkscrew Strike against it. If the Strike damages the target, the dig-widget attaches to the target (typically to the back of a creature). This is similar to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.Tkd8sH4pwFIPzqTr]{Grabbing} the creature, but the dig-widget moves with that creature rather than holding it in place. While attached, the dig-widget can't use its corkscrew. The dig-widget can be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.7blmbDrQFNfdT731]{Shoved} off, or it can detach itself with an Interact action.

Grind Bones.name: Grind Bones
Grind Bones.description:
Requirements A grinder-widget adjacent to the millstone in area C41 has a creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}

Effect The grinder-widget attaches pliers to one of the millstone's handles and Strides around it, causing the Grabbed character to be painfully ground and pulped by the stone. The ground character must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:23|options:damaging-effect,inflicts:clumsy] save with the following results.

Critical Success The character is unaffected and automatically Escapes from the grapple.

Success The character takes @Damage[(1d8+2)[bludgeoning]] damage and then automatically Escapes from the grapple.

Failure The character takes @Damage[(2d8+2)[bludgeoning]] damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} for 1 hour from wrenched and sprained limbs; the character remains grappled by the grinder-widget.

Critical Failure As failure, but @Damage[(4d8+2)[bludgeoning]] damage and clumsy 1 for 24 hours.

Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
Sneak Attack.description: A dig-widget's Strikes deal an additional 1d6 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

The Babies Are So Hungry.name: The Babies Are So Hungry
The Babies Are So Hungry.disable: @Check[nature|dc:33] (master) to use the dreamwell plant's own blooms to soothe the ghostly spiders or @Check[religion|dc:36] (trained) to exorcise the ghostly spiders; three successes are required to disable the haunt completely
The Babies Are So Hungry.hazarddescription: The dreamwell plant shudders and pulses, emitting more potent odors before it bursts into swarms of ravenous ghostly spiders.
The Babies Are So Hungry.routine:
(2 actions) An immense swarm of thumb-sized spiders boil out of the plant's planter box and its bulbous trunk, filling the air with the nauseating sound of tens of thousands of tiny clawed feet scuttling everywhere. The haunt uses its first action to spray webbing through the area so that every creature in the room must succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:30] save to avoid taking a –5-foot status penalty to their Speed. These penalties stack with multiple failed Reflex saves, and a character whose penalties reduce their Speed to 0 becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} ([[/act escape dc=30]]).

On its second action, the phantasmal spiders begin to bite and gnaw at living flesh with fangs that are suddenly both very real and very toxic. Every creature in the room takes 2d10 piercing and @Damage[2d10[poison]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:30|basic] save).
The Babies Are So Hungry.reset: The haunt deactivates at the end of any round in which there are no Small or larger living creatures in the room, then resets automatically.

Dreamtime Bloom.name: Dreamtime Bloom
Dreamtime Bloom.description:
Trigger A Small or larger living creature spends more than a minute in the room, or anyone attempts to move or damage the plant

Effect The dreamwell plant's flowers bloom and fill the air in area F14 with soporific scents. All creatures in the room must attempt a @Check[will|dc:30|options:inflicts:incapacitated,inflicts:slowed] save with the following effects; the haunt then rolls initiative.

Critical Success The character is unaffected.

Success The character takes a –1 status penalty to their initiative roll at the start of the following round.

Failure As success, but the character is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} from sudden tiredness. The affected character can attempt a new @Check[will|dc:30] save at the end of a round to recover from this condition; otherwise, it lasts for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The character falls @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious}. If it's still unconscious (and alive) after 1 hour, it wakes up automatically.

Arth Wiltur.name: Arth Wiltur
Arth Wiltur.allSaves: –2 status penalty to all saves vs. curses

–2 Status Penalty to All Saves vs. Curse.name: –2 Status Penalty to All Saves vs. Curses

Hooked.name: Hooked
Hooked.description: A creature struck by Arth's fish hook is skewered, taking @Damage[1d4[persistent,bleed]] damage as long as the hook remains stuck. A creature can [[/act escape dc=28]] from the hook.

Humiliate the Fish.name: Humiliate the Fish
Humiliate the Fish.description:
Requirements A creature is hooked by Arth's fish hook and adjacent to Arth

Effect Arth yanks the hook free, causing @Damage[4d8[slashing]] damage to the creature (@Check[fortitude|dc:28|basic|options:inflicts:prone] save), who also falls @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} if they fail that Fortitude save.

Reel In.name: Reel In
Reel In.description: Arth pulls the rope attached to his hook. If he has no creature hooked, the fish hook returns to his hand. If a creature is hooked, Arth attempts an @Check[athletics|against:fortitude|options:forced-movement] check against the creature's Fortitude DC, pulling it up to 30 feet closer on a success (60 feet on a critical success).

Swear.name: Swear
Swear.description: Arth unleashes a string of invectives. Each creature that hears him must attempt a @Check[will|dc:28|traits:concentrate,curse,manipulate] save, with the effects of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.z2mfh3oPnfYqXflY]{Mariner's Curse}, and is then temporarily immune for 24 hours. Even on a failed save, the curse ends automatically after 24 hours.

Religious Disgust.name: Religious Disgust
Religious Disgust.description: A character who openly wears religious iconography or the religious symbol of either Pharasma or Shelyn gains a +2 status bonus to their AC for attacks from Ryhasphinea. If a PC attempts to [[/act demoralize]] Ryhasphinea by invoking either deity, they can attempt to Demoralize with a Religion check instead of an Intimidation check. If she becomes frightened by this attempt, she also becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} as long as she remains frightened out of disgust.

Share Blessings.name: Share Blessings
Share Blessings.description: When Ryhasphinea is destroyed, she explodes in a blast of infectious rot. All creatures in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:10] are exposed to soulphage.

Feed the Dead.name: Feed the Dead
Feed the Dead.description:
Frequency once per minute

Requirements Ryhasphinea is adjacent to an undead creature

Effect Ryhasphinea siphons void energy into the undead creature, granting it 30 temporary Hit Points and making it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} for 3 rounds. The undead creature's temporary Hit Points last as long as it remains quickened, and it can use the extra action only to Stride or Strike.

Soulphage.name: Soulphage
Soulphage.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:33]

Stage 1 carrier (1 day)

Stage 2 @Damage[3d8[void]] damage and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1} (1 day)

Stage 3 @Damage[4d8[void]] damage, drained 1, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 2} (1 day)

Stage 4 @Damage[4d8[void]] damage, drained 1, enfeebled 2, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 3} (1 day)

Stage 5 @Damage[4d8[void]] damage, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 2}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 3}, clumsy 3, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 3}

Stage 6 dead. A creature that dies while infected with soulphage rises as a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core-2.Actor.ZQ7lS9TYOFv07m1a]{War Wraith}

Visceral Reap.name: Visceral Reap
Visceral Reap.description: Ryhasphinea makes a scything blade Strike and compares the attack roll result to the AC of up to two foes, each of whom must be within her melee reach. Roll damage only once, and apply it to each creature hit. The first creature damaged by Visceral Reap also takes @Damage[1d6[persistent,bleed]] damage. Reap counts as two attacks for Ryhasphinea's multiple attack penalty.

Spewing Honey.name: Spewing Honey
Spewing Honey.description: When Sovina takes slashing damage, her wound spews rancid honey mixed with bile on adjacent creatures, dealing @Damage[2d12[poison]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:22|basic|options:inflicts:slowed] save). A creature that fails this saving throw is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 round by the thick, sticky honey. Sovina loses her spewing honey and penanggalan bile abilities until the end of her next turn.

Elongate Tongue.name: Elongate Tongue
Elongate Tongue.description: The penanggalan's tongue extends, the membrane stretching and becoming translucent. Until the end of the turn, the penanggalan's proboscis tongue Strikes have a 10-foot reach, and any target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} against the Strike unless it has a Perception DC of 25 or higher or the ability to precisely sense @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible} things.

Penanggalan Bile.name: Penanggalan Bile
Penanggalan Bile.description:
Rest doesn't decrease the drained value from penanggalan bile

Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:22]

Stage 1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1} (1 week)

Stage 2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 2} (1 week)

Stage 3 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 3} (1 week)

Stage 4 dead

Ride Corpse.name: Ride Corpse
Ride Corpse.description:
The penanggalan inserts their entrails into their humanoid body, allowing them to appear as and move about like a normal human. The body has 10 Hit Points and the same defenses as the penanggalan.

When the body is destroyed, the penanggalan is ejected unharmed. The body becomes a corpse, and if it is neither controlled by the penanggalan nor stored in an alchemical vat, it decays as normal.

What All Heroes Fear.name: What All Heroes Fear
What All Heroes Fear.disable: @Check[intimidation|dc:25] to push back against the haunt with your own memories of bravery or @Check[religion|dc:28] to exorcise the haunt; three successes are required to disable it.
What All Heroes Fear.hazarddescription: The depictions of heroic deeds transform as the lights dim, becoming testaments to cowardice and failure.
What All Heroes Fear.routine:

Gogiteth (Bastion of Blasphemies).name: Gogiteth (Bastion of Blasphemies)
Gogiteth (Bastion of Blasphemies).publicNotes:
A gogiteth is a slavering nightmare of teeth, eyes, and hairy spiderlike legs, and its appearance is invariably seared into the minds of any who witness it. Hives of these skittering monsters haunt the lowest reaches of the Darklands, competing with cave worms and other subterranean horrors for food and resources. A gogiteth is rarely alone, as they learned that the best means of survival is sticking with others of their own kind. Even the hardiest Darklands residents seek cover when a gogiteth is spotted, for where there's one, a swarm is sure to follow.

Gogiteths make a clacking sound as they skitter. The joints in their many legs pop and crack with each movement, though they can suppress this voluntarily and hunt silently without alerting prey. The odd creatures can also make a high-pitched whistling sound that echoes throughout the caverns where they live. Some Darklands natives report that groups of gogiteths sometimes join together in eerie, discordant songs.

Gogiteth anatomy have inspired no shortage of speculation as to their origins. Some believe they are the result of a fleshwarping experiment gone horribly wrong. Others think they may be related in some way to the Dominion of the Black—possibly the distant cousins or some strange exiles of those alien entities. According to this mythos, once they made their way to Golarion, the gogiteths crawled into the depths of the earth, shying away from the blazing sun above.

Gogiteths are a menace to every other denizen of the Darklands. Those who live in gogiteth-infested regions of Sekamina or Orv frequently call for temporary truces when a gogiteth swarm has been spotted. Since even an average gogiteth hive can host up to two dozen of the horrors, calls to eradicate them are dangerous quests indeed.

Skittering Assault.description: The gogiteth Strides three times. Once per Stride, it can attempt a leg Strike against a creature in its reach at any point during the Stride; it must make each attack against a different creature, but it doesn't apply its multiple attack penalty until after making all its Strikes. If any of the Strikes result in a critical failure, Skittering Assault ends.

Sludge Troll.name: Sludge Troll
Sludge Troll.publicNotes:
The lanky, greasy sludge troll always seems to look like they just slid out of a pool of noxious sewage or filthy swamp water, with their scaly hide dripping with oily fluids and crusty muck. While they possess the iconic underbite and tusks of the typical troll, their facial features are much more fishlike, with bulging eyes and fin-like ridges on their spine, brow, and forearms. In addition to possessing prodigious regenerative qualities, sludge trolls are immune to diseases, and as a result, they often wallow and lair in areas infested with sickness for additional defenses. Tunnels and sewage outflows are their favored places to lurk in ambush, particularly if these areas see lots of traffic from underworld denizens. Generally more stealthy and sneaky than the typical troll, a sludge troll roused to violence is as terrifying and impossible to ignore as any others of their kind.

Sewer Dwellers

While sludge trolls are often found dwelling in mires and bogs, they are also perfectly at home lurking in sewers and cisterns below urban areas. Their lanky limbs and ability to squeeze through smaller areas helps them navigate confines that might prove troublesome for other creatures of their size, yet sewer-dwelling sludge trolls are still careful to avoid attracting too much attention from those in positions of power in the city above.

Easily Misled.name: Easily Misled
Easily Misled.description: The sludge troll gets a –4 circumstance penalty to their Perception DC against Deception checks.

Furious Spit.name: Furious Spit
Furious Spit.description:
Trigger The sludge troll takes cold or fire damage

Effect The sludge troll makes a sludge cough Strike against a random creature within their first range increment. If the troll is taking persistent fire damage, they attempt a @Check[flat|dc:15] to remove it.

Aquatic Upsurge.name: Aquatic Upsurge
Aquatic Upsurge.description:
Requirements The sludge troll is hiding in water, and a creature that hasn't detected it is within 30 feet

Effect The sludge troll Swims, then Leaps at the end of its Swim action, landing on any solid surface adjacent to the water. Once the triggering creature is in the troll's first range increment, the sludge troll makes a sludge cough Strike against the creature with a +2 circumstance bonus to the attack roll.

Blinding Sludge.name: Blinding Sludge
Blinding Sludge.description: A creature that is critically hit by a sludge troll's sludge cough becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} by the toxic sludge until it uses an Interact action to clear its eyes.

Flexible Limbs.name: Flexible Limbs
Flexible Limbs.description: A sludge troll's limbs and torso are eerily flexible. They can clamber and splash through difficult terrain caused by swamp features with ease (treating such areas as non-difficult terrain) as well as move through areas as if they were one size category smaller with ease (Medium, for the typical sludge troll).

Site Bound.name: Site Bound
Site Bound.description: A typical ghost can stray only a short distance from where it was killed or the place it haunts. A typical limit is 120 feet. Some ghosts are instead bound to a room, building, item, or creature that was special to it rather than a location.

Rejuvenation.name: Rejuvenation
Rejuvenation.description: If he's destroyed, he rejuvenates in [[/gmr 2d4 #days]]{2d4 days} unless the Bastardhall Curse is lifted.

Blasphemous Decree.name: Blasphemous Decree
Blasphemous Decree.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect Eragayl points out a creature he can see within 60 feet with his blade, proclaiming them to be heretics deserving of death. The target creature's faith quakes and strains under the decree, and the target creature must attempt a @Check[will|dc:29|options:damaging-effect,inflicts:stunned,inflicts:stupefied] save with the following effects. Worshippers of Shelyn gain a +2 status bonus to this saving throw. This ability replaces the ghost mage's arcane innate spells.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected. If the creature is a worshipper of Shelyn, Eragayl is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 3}.

Success The creature takes @Damage[2d8[mental]] damage.

Failure The creature takes @Damage[4d8[mental]] damage. If the creature can cast divine spells, it's @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} for 1 round.

Critical Failure The creature takes @Damage[8d8[mental]] damage. If the creature can cast divine spells, it is stupefied 1 for 1 round and can't cast divine spells for 1 round.

Frightful Moan.name: Frightful Moan
Frightful Moan.description: The ghost laments its fate, forcing each living creature within @Template[emanation|distance:30]{30 feet} to attempt a @Check[will|dc:29|options:area-effect,inflicts:frightened] save. On a failure, a creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} (or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} on a critical failure). On a success, a creature is temporarily immune to this ghost's frightful moan for 1 minute.

Reminders of Life.name: Reminders of Life
Reminders of Life.description: Eragayl is shocked if anyone addresses him by the nickname his wife Tasifinie had for him: "tiger." The first time someone does so in a round, Eragayl must attempt a @Check[will|dc:35] save to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 round by the distraction. If the person who used this name on him openly wields Fearcutter, his memories usurp his nature automatically; he shrieks in rage and turns his wrath on Irrokcis instead, cursing his son's name as he uses a combination of Blasphemous Decrees and Telekinetic Assault on the lich for the rest of the combat.

Telekinetic Assault.name: Telekinetic Assault
Telekinetic Assault.description: The ghost cries out in pain and anguish as small objects and debris fly about in a @Template[emanation|distance:30]. Creatures in this area take @Damage[6d6[bludgeoning]|options:area-damage] damage, subject to a @Check[reflex|dc:29|basic|options:area-effect] save.

Site Bound.name: Site Bound
Site Bound.description: These three ghosts can only leave the crypts when Bastardhall appears on Golarion, and even then, they can't leave the island.

Rejuvenation.name: Rejuvenation
Rejuvenation.description: The three adventurers re-form after [[/gmr 2d4 #days]]{2d4 days} here in the crypts unless someone carries their respective urn of ashes down to the temple in Maiserene (area A9) to be cleansed by Shirail.

Amondi's Cruel Shiv.name: Amondi's Cruel Shiv
Amondi's Cruel Shiv.description: Amondi Flies once, moving through a target creature's space; this movement doesn't trigger reactions. As she moves through the target's space, she makes a ghostly weapon Strike against the target. If she hits, she deals an additional @Damage[3d6[persistent,bleed]] damage, and the creature struck becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} from the pain of the bloody wound.

Malevolent Possession.name: Malevolent Possession
Malevolent Possession.description: The ghost attempts to possess an adjacent corporeal creature. This has the same effect as the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.wU6hNzK8Yfqdmc8m]{Possession} spell (@Check[will|dc:23]), except since the ghost doesn't have a physical body, it is unaffected by that restriction of the spell.

Site Bound.name: Site Bound
Site Bound.description: The ghostly guests cannot leave the reception halls.

Rejuvenation.name: Rejuvenation
Rejuvenation.description: When a ghostly guest is destroyed, they reform after [[/gmr 2d4 #days]]{2d4 days} fully healed and can be encountered again. They're only permanently destroyed once the Bastardhall Curse is lifted at the end of the Adventure Path.

Join Us!.name: Join Us!
Join Us!.description:
The ghostly guest Flies over to a space adjacent to a creature, then extends their arms in an invitation to join the ghost in whatever form of revelry it appears to be engaged in at the moment, be it dancing, drinking, or eating. The target must attempt a @Check[will|dc:24] save to resist the invitation. On a failed save, roll [[/gmr 1d6#Revelry]] to determine what the ghost's current revelry is and what effect the creature endures. If the target fails its save against Join Us! while already enduring a condition inflicted by a previous failed save, the new condition replaces the old condition, and the change in condition leaves the character @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} for 1 round from the disorienting sensations.

1–2 Dancing The creature suddenly feels as if they've been dancing the night away. Aches and pains settle into their bodies, and they become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 2} on a critical failure) for 1 hour.

3–4 Drinking The creature suddenly feels dizzy and drunk and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} on a critical failure) for 1 hour.

5–6 Eating The creature suddenly feels bloated and overfull and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} on a critical failure) for 1 hour.

Bring Dusk to Dawn.hazarddescription: Shadows rise up from the empty tub, creeping along the floor, walls, and celling to blot out light.
Bring Dusk to Dawn.routine: (2 actions) A shadowy figure rises up from the bath, resembling the upper torso of a demonic humanoid with glowing eyes. On its first action, the haunt sweeps its many arms through area A19, dealing @Damage[4d6[void]] damage on all living creatures in the area (@Check[fortitude|dc:21|basic] save). On its second action, it either spawns an undead shadow from its mass, or it Sustains a currently spawned undead shadow; it can only have one shadow active at a time. This shadow has the minion trait, cannot leave area A19, and takes its two actions on the haunt's initiative. Void damage from the haunt doesn't heal a shadow minion.
Bring Dusk to Dawn.reset: The haunt deactivates at the end of any round in which no living creature is in area A19, then resets 1 round later.

Shadows Rise.name: Shadows Rise
Shadows Rise.description:
Trigger More than three living creatures end their turn in area A19 or any one creature ends their turn while standing within the empty bath

Effect Shadows seep out from the bath and swiftly coat the walls and ceiling, covering all entrances into A19 with sheets of shadow, plunging the area within into darkness. Non-magical light sources, such as a torch or lantern, do not emanate any light in the room while the haunt is active. This also suppresses magical light of rank 3 or lower. The haunt then rolls initiative.

equipment-Soulheart.name: Soulheart
equipment-Soulheart.description:
A soulheart is a crystallized sphere of red ectoplasm about the size of a human eye. When held by a living creature, a faint red light shimmers within the crystal, pulsating in a synchronized beat with the creature's heartbeat and providing illumination equivalent to that of a candle.

Activate—Bolster Life 2 (concentrate, manipulate)

Frequency once per day

Effect When held to the chest and focused upon, the soul energy within the soulheart floods outward and bolsters your life force, granting you 6 temporary Hit Points (or 3 temporary Hit Points if it's nighttime). These temporary Hit Points last for 8 hours.

Activate—Bolster Maiserene Phantom 2 (concentrate, manipulate)

Effect When touched to a rank 0 Maiserene phantom, the soulheart flashes with bright red light and is destroyed. As it does so, it permanently increases the targeted phantom to rank 1, and increases each PC's maximum Hit Points by 1 for as long as they remain within Bastardhall while the castle remains cursed.

Destruction A soulheart is destroyed when it is activated to Bolster Maiserene Phantom.

Red Cap.name: Red Cap
Red Cap.description:
A redcap's woolen hat is dyed with the blood of their victims. If the redcap loses their cap, they no longer benefit from fast healing and take a –4 status penalty to their damage rolls. They can create a new cap in 10 minutes, but that cap doesn't grant them powers until the redcap has turned it red with Blood Soak. A cap has no benefit for creatures other than the redcap who made it.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.s5mS7CyE0oOYlecv]{Effect: Lost Red Cap}

Bolster Life.name: Bolster Life
Bolster Life.description:
Frequency once per day

Effect When held to the chest and focused upon, the soul energy within the soulheart floods outward and bolsters your life force, granting you 6 temporary Hit Points (or 3 temporary Hit Points if it's nighttime). These temporary Hit Points last for 8 hours.

Divine Revulsion.name: Divine Revulsion
Divine Revulsion.description:
If a redcap sees a creature brandish a religious symbol of a deity (which requires an Interact action by that creature) or cast a divine spell while wearing a religious symbol, the redcap must attempt a @Check[will|dc:24] save. The DC is @Check[will|dc:26] against a symbol of Shelyn and @Check[will|dc:34] against his lucky dawnsilver corkscrew.

They then become temporarily immune to all brandished religious symbols for 10 minutes.

Critical Success The redcap is unaffected.

Success The redcap is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Failure The redcap gains the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} condition for 1 round and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 4}.

Sommelier's Mockery.name: Sommelier's Mockery
Sommelier's Mockery.description:
Trigger A creature Brensen can see within 30 feet spends an action retching in an attempt to recover from the sickened condition and fails

Effect Brensen points and laughs at the triggering creature, causing their sickened condition value to increase by 1, or to fall @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} if their sickened condition value is already @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 3}.

Soak Cap.name: Soak Cap
Soak Cap.description:
Brensen dips his cap into red wine or blood from a slain foe. Wine must have been opened by Brensen within the last minute. Blood must be from a creature Brensen helped kill and must have died within the last minute. He gains a +4 status bonus to damage rolls and Fortitude saves for 1 minute.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.wPIGBcpCqCWgrCiq]{Effect: Blood Soak}

Sommelier's Trick.name: Sommelier's Trick
Sommelier's Trick.description:
Brensen takes a deep gulp of alcohol, then winks at a creature he can see within 30 feet. The alcohol he imbibed suddenly infuses the belly of the target, causing them to attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:25] save with the following effects.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}.

Failure The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} and falls @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} as long as it's remain sickened.

Stomp.name: Stomp
Stomp.description: The redcap Strides up to half its Speed and makes a boot Strike at any point during that movement. If the boot Strike hits a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} creature, it deals an extra @Damage[2d6[bleed]].

No Light Shall Guide Thee.name: No Light Shall Guide Thee
No Light Shall Guide Thee.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:30] (master) to subtly sift the ashes aside in a way where the curse simply fades without discerning a target or @Check[occultism|dc:33] (expert) to know how to harmlessly disperse the malign magic
No Light Shall Guide Thee.hazarddescription: The evercursed crystals suddenly extinguish if they are disturbed, taking the PCs' sight away with their failing light.

Devour Sight.name: Devour Sight
Devour Sight.description:
Trigger A creature disturbs the ashes in the fireplace or attempts to manipulate any of the evercursed crystals

Effect The crystals burn out, becoming non-magical stones, and the triggering creature must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:32|options:inflicts:dazzled,inflicts:blinded] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature's vision blurs and dims, and they become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} for 24 hours.

Failure As success, but with an unlimited duration.

Critical Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} with an unlimited duration.

Vink Cratched.name: Vink Cratched
Vink Cratched.publicNotes:
The lanky, greasy sludge troll always seems to look like they just slid out of a pool of noxious sewage or filthy swamp water, with their scaly hide dripping with oily fluids and crusty muck. While they possess the iconic underbite and tusks of the typical troll, their facial features are much more fishlike, with bulging eyes and fin-like ridges on their spine, brow, and forearms. In addition to possessing prodigious regenerative qualities, sludge trolls are immune to diseases, and as a result, they often wallow and lair in areas infested with sickness for additional defenses. Tunnels and sewage outflows are their favored places to lurk in ambush, particularly if these areas see lots of traffic from underworld denizens. Generally more stealthy and sneaky than the typical troll, a sludge troll roused to violence is as terrifying and impossible to ignore as any others of their kind.

Sewer Dwellers

While sludge trolls are often found dwelling in mires and bogs, they are also perfectly at home lurking in sewers and cisterns below urban areas. Their lanky limbs and ability to squeeze through smaller areas helps them navigate confines that might prove troublesome for other creatures of their size, yet sewer-dwelling sludge trolls are still careful to avoid attracting too much attention from those in positions of power in the city above.

Easily Misled.name: Easily Misled
Easily Misled.description: The sludge troll gets a –4 circumstance penalty to their Perception DC against Deception checks.

Furious Spit.name: Furious Spit
Furious Spit.description:
Trigger The sludge troll takes cold or fire damage

Effect The sludge troll makes a sludge cough Strike against a random creature within their first range increment. If the troll is taking persistent fire damage, they attempt a @Check[flat|dc:15] to remove it.

Aquatic Upsurge.name: Aquatic Upsurge
Aquatic Upsurge.description:
Requirements The sludge troll is hiding in water, and a creature that hasn't detected it is within 30 feet

Effect The sludge troll Swims, then Leaps at the end of its Swim action, landing on any solid surface adjacent to the water. Once the triggering creature is in the troll's first range increment, the sludge troll makes a sludge cough Strike against the creature with a +2 circumstance bonus to the attack roll.

Blinding Sludge.name: Blinding Sludge
Blinding Sludge.description: A creature that is critically hit by a sludge troll's sludge cough becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} by the toxic sludge until it uses an Interact action to clear its eyes.

Goading Roar.name: Goading Roar
Goading Roar.description: Vink unleashes a gurgling, sputtering roar that sounds as if it issues from a throat partially clogged with mud. The sputtering sound isn't particularly frightening, but it compels other sludge trolls within 30 feet to grow more frenzied. All sludge trolls who hear Vink's Goading Roar become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} for 1 round, and may use the extra action to Stride or Swim.

Despair is thy Reward.name: Despair is thy Reward
Despair is thy Reward.disable: @Check[intimidation|dc:26] (trained) to stand firm against the coming terrors and show no fear or @Check[religion|dc:23] (expert) to exorcise the haunt; two total successes are required to disable the haunt
Despair is thy Reward.hazarddescription: The ghosts of weeping, cowardly soldiers and the sound of claws scraping on the outer walls manifest.
Despair is thy Reward.routine: (1 action) The sound of talons scratching on the outer walls of the room and glimpses of lean, shadowy shapes flapping and scrambling at the arrow slits manifest. A PC who takes an action to [[/act seek]] these shapes and succeeds at a DC 21 Occultism check to [[/act recall-knowledge skill=occultism dc=21]] recognizes the shapes as nightgaunts. Each round on its turn, these shadowy nightgaunts reach impossibly long, thin, spade-tipped tails into the room through the arrow slits or down the stove's chimney to make a shadowy tail Strike against every creature in the room as 1 action. If the door to this area remains open, the tails have an easier time reaching inside and gain a +2 circumstance bonus on their attack rolls.
Despair is thy Reward.reset: The haunt deactivates and then resets after 1 round in which no living creatures are within the watch post.

They're All Around Us!.name: They're All Around Us!
They're All Around Us!.description:
Trigger A living creature ends their turn inside the watch post

Effect Ghostly human soldiers manifest in the central alcove, crying out in terror as they drop their weapons and beg for mercy. Each PC in area A3 becomes overwhelmed with the conviction that their own battle prowess will not save them from the danger rushing toward the building and must attempt a @Check[will|dc:22|options:area-effect,inflicts:frightened] save to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} on a critical failure). The haunt then rolls initiative.

Tickle.name: Tickle
Tickle.description: A creature that takes damage from a shadowy tail is uncomfortably tickled by the slithering appendage and must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:21|options:inflicts:sickened] save to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} on a critical failure).

Personality Fragments.name: Personality Fragments
Personality Fragments.description:
A soulbound doll shares fragments of its donor soul's personality, though none of that creature's memories. This causes a soulbound doll to match a strong personality trait of the donor soul. Because of its soul sliver, a soulbound doll is not immune to spirit as most constructs are.

When Grampa Sizzle casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Jmxru8zMdYMRuO5n]{Vision of Death}, targets experience the terror of burning alive, and when he casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.R8bqnYiThB6MYTxD]{Phantom Pain}, the targets suddenly recall painful burns.

Pratfall.name: Pratfall
Pratfall.description:
Trigger Grampa Sizzle fails or critically fails an attack roll or a skill check

Effect Grampa Sizzle makes a quick scene out of his failure, such as by falling and suddenly bouncing back to his feet or making a ridiculous face. If he has a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.tlSE7Ly8vi1Dgddv]{Laughing Fit} spell available, he can cast it as part of this reaction.

Trapped Arudora Soul.name: Trapped Arudora Soul
Trapped Arudora Soul.disable:
@Check[religion|dc:41] to exorcise the haunt, or one of the following checks depending on the Arudora; four total successes are required to disable the haunt.

J3a (Jinnivere) @Check[nature|dc:38] to draw upon her love of horses

J3b (Dazerien) @Check[intimidation|dc:38] to frighten the cruel murderer

J3c (Ryhasphinea) @Check[deception|dc:38] to trick her into believing she's been forsaken by Urgathoa

J3d (Augsten) @Check[diplomacy|dc:38] to explain that abuse of the servants shows weakness of character

J3e (Alisendra) @Check[performance|dc:38] to give her one last entertainment

J3f (Raudltz) @Check[society|dc:38] to help him come to terms with the shame he feels for his infidelities

J3g (Irrokcis) @Check[occultism|dc:38] to use his own obscure theories against him to banish him
Trapped Arudora Soul.hazarddescription: A ghostly image of one of the Arudoras floats in the middle of the room, arms folded over their chest as if reclining in a coffin, yet they hover vertically and are shrouded by ribbons of green smoke.
Trapped Arudora Soul.routine:
(1 action) On its initiative, the haunt transforms into a physical manifestation of that Arudora's personality and lashes out, dealing @Damage[9d6[untyped]] damage to all creatures in the room and within 30 feet of any open doorway outside the room. A PC can attempt a DC 34 basic saving throw against the damage. The type of damage and saving throw to defend against it depend on the Arudora, as does the additional condition imparted on a critical failure. Conditions imparted by this haunt are curses that have unlimited durations.

J3a (Jinnivere) trampling horses (bludgeoning damage, Reflex save, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} on a critical failure)

J3b (Dazerien) complex torture devices (piercing damage, Reflex save, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} on a critical failure)

J3c (Ryhasphinea) skull-faced spirits (spirit damage, Will save, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} on a critical failure)

J3d (Augsten) barbed whip and scourge Strikes (slashing damage, Reflex save, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} on a critical failure)

J3e (Alisendra) shrieking spirits and discordant instruments (sonic damage, Fortitude save, stupefied 1 on a critical failure)

J3f (Raudltz) ghostly fangs that chew into your thoughts (mental damage, Will save, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1} on a critical failure)

J3g (Irrokcis) decaying skeletal limbs (void damage, Fortitude save, drained 1 on a critical failure)
Trapped Arudora Soul.reset: The haunt deactivates as soon as no living creatures are in the room, then immediately resets.
Trapped Arudora Soul.stealthdetails: (master) to notice that the eerie manifestation is dangerous; noticing the ghostly image of the Arudora in question floating in the middle of the room has a DC of 0

Awaken.name: Awaken
Awaken.description:
Trigger A living creature ends their turn in the room

Effect The soul's eyes open, and it cries out in agony as its ghostly body twists and transforms into something monstrous. The triggering PC must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:34|options:inflicts:frightened,inflicts:fleeing] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for as long as they're frightened on a critical failure). The haunt then rolls initiative.

Velicarn (Dullahan).name: Velicarn (Dullahan)
Velicarn (Dullahan).publicNotes:
Riding on a horse as black as night, the headless hunter known as the dullahan tracks down and takes the heads of those they deem unfit to continue living. When closing in for the kill, the dullahan first whispers their victim's name, then swiftly collects their prize, casting a pall of dread upon all who witness the grim execution.

A dullahan manifests when a particularly violent warrior is beheaded and the warrior's soul stubbornly clings to material existence (or is refused entry to the afterlife). Most dullahans return to their former homelands, where they can exact vengeance on those they feel wronged them in life (or their living descendants). A dullahan's concept of justice is swift and merciless, and once they've selected a target, they're unwavering in their cause.

Perhaps even more than revenge, a dullahan desires their own rotted head. An individual who wields the head of a dullahan is powerful indeed, for a dullahan will grudgingly serve such a master in the hopes of reclaiming their missing skull. Mighty fiends such as devils command dullahans to harvest souls or lead armies for them, while a mortal might use such an undead warrior to fulfill a personal vendetta. A dullahan won't hesitate to kill their liege and reclaim their head when the opportunity presents itself.

Bastard's Shame.name: Bastard's Shame
Bastard's Shame.description:
Velicarn harbors deep feelings of shame and anger about his heritage, and a PC can capitalize on this to insult him or to distract him as follows.

Insult Velicarn The PC attempts a @Check[intimidation|dc:30] check to [[/act demoralize]] Velicarn. On a critical success, he's also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} by his anger for 1 round. If he's also already @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} as a result of being distracted, he takes @Damage[6d6[mental]] damage (@Check[will|dc:30|basic] save) on a success (@Damage[12d6[mental]] damage on a critical success).

Distract Velicarn The PC attempts a @Check[deception|dc:28] check to [[/act feint]] Velicarn. On a critical success, he's also slowed 1 by his anger for 1 round. If he's also already slowed as a result of being insulted, he takes @Damage[6d6[mental]] damage (@Check[will|dc:30|basic] save) on a success (@Damage[12d6[mental]] damage on a critical success).

Head Hunter.name: Head Hunter
Head Hunter.description: Any slashing weapon gains the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.hg3IogR8ue2IWwgS]{Keen} rune while a dullahan wields it, and any hatchet they wield gains the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.qlunQzfnzPQpMG6U]{Returning} rune as well. If the dullahan kills a creature with a critical hit using a slashing weapon, the target is decapitated as though the dullahan had used Reap on the target.

Reap.name: Reap
Reap.description: The dullahan removes the head of a dead creature within reach. Each creature within the area of the dullahan's frightful presence must attempt a new save, even if it is temporarily immune.

Summon Steed.name: Summon Steed
Summon Steed.description: The dullahan summons a war horse with elite adjustments and the fiend and unholy traits. This steed remains until it is slain, the dullahan Dismisses this effect, or the dullahan Summons a Steed again.

Let My Torments Be Yours.name: Let My Torments Be Yours
Let My Torments Be Yours.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:32] (master) to carefully remove the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.JmlPFAbjPvbhhKeu]{Vile Remnant} from the skeleton's ribcage without triggering the haunt or @Check[religion|dc:35] (expert) to exorcise the haunt
Let My Torments Be Yours.hazarddescription: The skeleton suddenly appears to lurch forward, crying out in pain as a shaking voice begs for someone to take away the pain.

A Gift of Torment.name: A Gift of Torment
A Gift of Torment.description:
Trigger A creature attacks the skeleton or ends their turn adjacent to the remains

Effect The skeleton lurches to unlife just long enough to beg for peace, then exhales at the triggering creature, who must attempt a @Check[will|dc:33] save or be subjected to the haunt's curse. A cursed creature becomes racked with pain from what feels like hours spent under a torturer's knives and takes a –1 status penalty to Fortitude saves. In addition, each time the creature takes slashing or piercing damage, they must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:33] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} from the agony (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} on a critical failure). The curse remains until removed by @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.SUKaxVZW2TlM8lu0]{Cleanse Affliction} or similar magic.

Amyleda Blackwell.name: Amyleda Blackwell
Amyleda Blackwell.allSaves: +1 status to all saves vs. magic

+1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic

Rejection Vulnerability.name: Rejection Vulnerability
Rejection Vulnerability.description:
As succubi are beings of pure lust, creatures that reject their lust can metaphysically harm them. When a succubus fails a Diplomacy check to Embrace or Request, or when a creature succeeds at its save against a succubus's mental spell or ability, the succubus takes @Damage[2d8[mental]] damage.

For 1 hour after causing mental damage to a succubus in this way, a creature can deal @Damage[2d8[mental]] damage to the succubus with a successful @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2u915NdUyQan6uKF]{Demoralize} action incorporating its rejection.

Seductive Presence.name: Seductive Presence
Seductive Presence.description:
10 feet.

Any creature in the aura that could be sexually attracted to a succubus takes a –2 circumstance penalty to checks and DCs to oppose the succubus's mental spells, Deception, and Diplomacy.

Change Shape.name: Change Shape
Change Shape.description:
The succubus can take on the appearance of any Small or Medium humanoid. This doesn't change their Speed or their attack and damage modifiers with their Strikes, but it might change the damage type their Strikes deal (typically to bludgeoning).

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ChangeShape]

Embrace.name: Embrace
Embrace.description: The succubus attempts to [[/act grapple skill=diplomacy]]{Grapple} a creature using their Diplomacy bonus instead of Athletics. If the creature is willing, the succubus automatically succeeds.

Passionate Kiss.name: Passionate Kiss
Passionate Kiss.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The succubus engages a creature they have @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} in an embrace or other act of passion to drain its vital essence.

The kiss makes the creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1} or increases its drained value by 1, to a maximum of 4. The creature takes @Damage[3d6[void]] damage and the succubus regains Hit Points equal to the damage dealt. The target must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:28] save or be affected by a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.qwlh6aDgi86U3Q7H]{Suggestion} to submit to more actions of passion rather than trying to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SkZAQRkLLkmBQNB9]{Escape}.

Profane Gift.name: Profane Gift
Profane Gift.description:
Frequency once per day

Effect The succubus gives a willing humanoid a profane gift. That creature gains a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, skill checks, and saving throws. As long as the gift persists, the succubus can communicate telepathically with the target at any distance, see through the creature's senses, and target the creature with suggestion through the telepathic link. In addition, the creature uses an outcome one degree of success worse than it rolls on saving throws against the succubus's @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.qwlh6aDgi86U3Q7H]{Suggestion} spells.

A humanoid can't have more than one profane gift at a time, and a succubus can't grant more than one profane gift at a time. Removing the gift requires an atone ritual. The succubus can remove the gift as a free action to give the recipient a curse, making them @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 3} with an unlimited duration.

A summoned succubus can't grant a profane gift.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.g5Yen1FhEMCzCJkv]{Effect: Profane Gift}

Spiritual Anguish.name: Spiritual Anguish
Spiritual Anguish.description:
Amyleda gives a creature within 30 feet a wistful smile, then instills within their mind the sudden conviction that someone who loved them in the past has either betrayed them or died. The targeted creature takes @Damage[8d6[mental]] damage and must attempt a @Check[will|dc:28|options:damaging-effect,inflicts:stupefied] save. Amyleda can't use Spiritual Anguish again for 1 hour or until she gives a creature a Passionate Kiss—whichever comes first.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune for 24 hours.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} by the distraction for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and is stupefied 1 from the distraction for 24 hours.

Vile Brew.name: Vile Brew
Vile Brew.disable: @Check[crafting|dc:28] (master) to swiftly dismantle key parts of the contraption containing the vile brew, or @Check[religion|dc:31] (expert) to exorcise the haunt; three total successes in all are needed to disable the haunt
Vile Brew.hazarddescription: The brewing equipment begins to shudder and shake, and thick foamy sludge starts to bubble up out of the various pipes, tuns, and barrels—sludge that contains blinking eyes, screaming mouths, and twitching fingers among its turbulent mass!
Vile Brew.routine: (3 actions) On its initiative, the churning awfulness extrudes a long, slimy tendril of clotted blood, tangled hair, and jagged broken teeth. These long, whiplike lengths then make three vile lash Strikes on three randomly determined targets in the room. With their reach and ability to manifest from any part of the machinery, these Strikes can target any creature in the room. They only target a creature more than once if there's not enough targets to split their attention.
Vile Brew.reset: The haunt deactivates at the start of any round in which no living creatures are in the room; it then reactivates 1 minute later.

Nightmare Recrudescence.name: Nightmare Recrudescence
Nightmare Recrudescence.description:
Trigger A creature attempts to use the brewing equipment, or at least one living creature spends 1 minute in the room

Effect The brewing equipment rattles to life as a hideous mash of what looks like clotted blood and body parts surges up and out of the machinery, pushing a nauseating stench into the room. All creatures in area C46 must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:26|options:inflicts:sickened] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} on a critical failure). The haunt then rolls initiative.

Flesh Fermentation.name: Flesh Fermentation
Flesh Fermentation.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:26|options:damaging-effect,inflicts:drained,inflicts:enfeebled]

Maximum Duration 6 rounds

Stage 1 @Damage[1d6[poison]] damage and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} (1 round)

Stage 2 @Damage[2d6[poison]] damage and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 2} (1 round)

Stage 3 @Damage[2d6[poison]] damage, enfeebled 2 (1 round), and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1}

The Bastard's Portrait.name: The Bastard's Portrait
The Bastard's Portrait.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:31] (trained) to carefully dismantle the portrait without jostling it enough to trigger it or @Check[religion|dc:33] (expert) to exorcise the haunt; 3 successes are required to disable it.
The Bastard's Portrait.hazarddescription: A mysterious portrait lies face down on the floor.

You Will Know My Name!.name: You Will Know My Name!
You Will Know My Name!.description:
Trigger A creature attempts to move the portrait

Effect Once someone flips the portrait over, they see a headless man portrayed in fine clothing, only to have the name "VELICARN" appear across the portrait in the form of bloody letters that run from the headless man's raw stump. If the triggering creature didn't attempt to look at the portrait, the painting wrenches and twists to present itself to the target, who must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:28] save to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} on a critical failure). A moment later, a trio of shadowy forms that drip and splatter blood surge out from the portrait, leaving it a blank canvas. These shapes appear vaguely as headless humanoids made of red smoke and leave bloodstains wherever they touch, but they're otherwise treated as typical wraiths. The wraiths roll initiative and remain for 1 minute, after which they vanish, and the portrait becomes a blank but bloodstained canvas. The wraiths also vanish if someone disables the haunt before the duration expires.

Raudltz Arudora.name: Raudltz Arudora
Raudltz Arudora.hp: coffin restoration, fast healing 10, void healing

Children of the Night.name: Children of the Night
Children of the Night.description:
Raudltz's ability to issue telepathic orders extends throughout the private halls and can be issued to any of his vampiric "children."

The vampire's presence brings forth creatures of the night to do the master's bidding. These typically include @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core.Actor.6wPW2dvpt86Ou6bL]{Rat Swarms}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core.Actor.2mg30nJR6P3HJDSd]{Bat Swarms}, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core.Actor.BN5Lb6IsQ9Wyu3rL]{Wolves}, but can include other creatures.

The vampire can give telepathic orders to these creatures as long as they are within 100 feet, but they can't communicate back.

Coffin Restoration.name: Coffin Restoration
Coffin Restoration.description: Unlike other undead, a vampire isn't destroyed at 0 HP. Instead, it falls @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious}. If its body rests in its coffin for 1 hour, the vampire gains 1 HP, after which its fast healing begins to function normally.

Mist Escape.name: Mist Escape
Mist Escape.description:
Trigger The vampire is reduced to 0 HP.

Effect The vampire uses Turn to Mist. They can take move actions to move toward its coffin even though it's at 0 HP. While at 0 HP in this form, the vampire is unaffected by further damage.

They automatically returns to its corporeal form, unconscious, if they reaches their coffin or after 2 hours, whichever comes first.

Vampire Vulnerabilities.name: Vampire Vulnerabilities
Vampire Vulnerabilities.description:
As vampire, but Raudltz is particularly sensitive if anyone even hints at the idea that not all of his children are legitimate heirs to the Arudora fortune and name. Any attempt to [[/act demoralize]] or [[/act feint]] against Raudltz that incorporates the linguistic trait and taunts him about rumors of illegitimate children gain a +2 circumstance bonus to the check. On a success, Raudltz is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} for 1 round in addition to the other effects (stupefied 1 for 1 minute on a critical success). If he has any dominated PCs at this time, each dominated PC can attempt a new saving throw against Dominate to end the effect early, but no more often than once per round.

All vampires possess the following vulnerabilities.

  • Compulsions Vampires are creatures with strange and unknowable compulsions. A typical vampire can't voluntarily cross running water unless they're transported while they hide within their coffin, nor can they enter a private dwelling unless invited in by someone with the authority to do so. At your discretion, vampires might have different compulsions—a pirate vampire might not be able to set foot on solid ground without being invited, for example. The vampire can still be forced to do these things and might be able to overcome their compulsion just as they do their revulsion.

  • Revulsion A vampire can't voluntarily come within 10 feet of brandished garlic or a brandished religious symbol of a deity with a holy sanctification option. To brandish garlic or a religious symbol, a creature must Interact to do so, and it remains brandished for 1 round (similar to Raising a Shield). If the vampire involuntarily comes within 10 feet of an object of their revulsion, they gain the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} condition, running from the object of their revulsion until they end an action beyond 10 feet. After 1 round of being exposed to the subject of their revulsion, a vampire can attempt a @Check[will|dc:25] save as a single action, which has the concentrate trait. On a success, they overcome their revulsions for [[/gmr 1d6 #rounds]]{1d6 rounds} (or 1 hour on a critical success).

  • Stake A wooden stake driven through a vampire's heart drops the vampire to 0 HP and prevents them from healing above 0 HP, even in their coffin. Staking a vampire requires 3 actions and works only if the vampire is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious}. If the stake is removed, the vampire can heal above 0 HP again, and if they're in their coffin, the 1-hour rest period begins once the stake is removed. If the vampire's head is severed and anointed with holy water while the stake is in place, the vampire is destroyed.

  • Sunlight If exposed to direct sunlight, a vampire immediately becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1}. The slowed value increases by 1 each time the vampire ends their turn in sunlight, and the condition ends when they're no longer in sunlight. If the vampire loses all their actions in this way, they're destroyed. Due to their supernatural aversion to light, vampires don't cast shadows or show a reflection in mirrors

Create Servitor.name: Create Servitor
Create Servitor.description:
If a creature dies after being reduced to 0 HP by Drink Blood, the vampire can turn this victim into a vampire servitor by donating some of their own blood to the victim and burying the victim in earth for 3 nights.

A vampiric servitor is compelled to obey its creator, but if a vampire controls too many vampiric servitors at once (as determined by the GM), or if the servitor is a higher level than the vampire that created it, strong-willed servitors can free themselves by succeeding at a @Check[will|defense:will] saving throw against the vampire's Will DC.

Dominate.name: Dominate
Dominate.description:
The vampire can cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.OsOhx3TGIZ7AhD0P]{Dominate} at will as a divine innate spell. Casting it requires staring into the target's eyes, giving the spell the visual trait (@Check[will|dc:]). The save DC uses the high spell DC of the vampire's level, and a creature that succeeds is temporarily immune to that vampire's Dominate for 24 hours.

Fully destroying the vampire ends the domination, but merely reducing the vampire to 0 HP is insufficient to break the spell.

Drink Blood.name: Drink Blood
Drink Blood.description:
Requirement A @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious}, or willing creature is within the vampire's reach.

Effect The vampire sinks its fangs into that creature to drink its blood. This requires an @Check[athletics|defense:fortitude] check against the victim's Fortitude DC if the victim is grabbed and is automatic for any of the other conditions.

The victim is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 2} and the vampire regains @Damage[16[healing]] HP, gaining any excess HP as temporary Hit Points. Drinking Blood from a creature that's already drained doesn't restore any HP to the vampire but increases the victim's drained value by 1, killing the victim when it reaches drained 5. A vampire can also consume blood that's been emptied into a vessel for sustenance, but it gains no HP from doing so.

A victim's drained condition decreases by 1 per week. A blood transfusion, which requires a @Check[medicine|dc:20|name:Blood Transfusion] check and sufficient blood or a blood donor, reduces the drain by 1 after 10 minutes.

Turn to Mist.name: Turn to Mist
Turn to Mist.description:
The vampire turns into a cloud of vapor, as the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.V8wXOsoejQhe6CyG]{Vapor Form} spell, or back to its normal form. The vampire loses fast healing while in gaseous form.

The vampire can remain in this form indefinitely.

Bloodsense (Imprecise) 90 feet.name: Bloodsense (Imprecise) 90 feet
Bloodsense (Imprecise) 90 feet.description: A blood hag can sense the presence of blood and creatures with blood. They can tell the difference between spilled blood and the blood within a living creature.

Borrowed Skin.name: Borrowed Skin
Borrowed Skin.description:
Alisandra's "borrowed skin" is her own skin from her previous life.

A blood hag wears a covering of skin stolen from a humanoid creature they've killed, hiding their true form. They appear as the creature whose skin they're wearing, including to spells that would detect that creature. Creatures can still potentially detect the deception as described in the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.AJstokjdG6iDjVjE]{Impersonate} action.

Spreading coarse salt inside the skin prevents the hag from putting it back on, forcing them to keep their fiery form until they kill another humanoid and spend 1 hour turning it into a new disguise.

Coven.name: Coven
Coven.description: Although Alisendra is on her own, the ambient energies of the Bastardhall Curse bolster her as if she were a part of a coven.
