She adds @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Uqj344bezBq3ESdq]{Nightmare}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.KSAEhNfZyXMO7Z7V]{Outcast's Curse}, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.r784cIz17eWujtQj]{Scrying} to her innate spells.

Assume Fiery Form.name: Assume Fiery Form
Assume Fiery Form.description:
The blood hag removes their borrowed skin and transforms into a brilliant ball of fire. They become amorphous (allowing them to move through a gap at least 1 foot wide without Squeezing and move at full Speed while Squeezing), gain the fire trait and a fly Speed of 60 feet, become immune to fire, and emit light as a torch. They lose their melee Strikes and can't Drain Blood, but they deal @Damage[4d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage with a @Check[reflex|dc:29|basic] save to each creature that touches them, including a creature that hits them with an unarmed attack or a weapon attack from an adjacent space. If their skin is intact and they're adjacent to it, they can Interact to return to their normal form inside the skin.

The hag can choose to Assume Fiery Form as a single action, bursting through their skin in a blast of flames. Doing so destroys their borrowed skin and deals @Damage[9d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage to all creatures in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:20] with a @Check[reflex|dc:26|basic] save.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.H99PJXU5cvJ4Oycm]{Effect: Fiery Form}

Drain Blood.name: Drain Blood
Drain Blood.description:
Requirements A @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious}, or willing creature is within the blood hag's reach

Effect The hag sinks their fangs into the creature to drink its blood. This requires a successful @Check[athletics|against:fortitude] check against the victim's Fortitude DC if the victim is grabbed and is automatic for any of the other conditions. The victim becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1}. The hag regains @Damage[15[healing]] Hit Points, gaining any excess HP as temporary Hit Points that last for 1 hour. Drinking blood from a creature that's already drained doesn't restore any Hit Points to the hag but increases the victim's drained value by 1, killing the victim when it reaches drained 5.

A victim's drained condition decreases by 1 per week. A blood transfusion, which requires a successful @Check[medicine|dc:20] check and sufficient blood or a blood donor, reduces the drained condition by 1 after 10 minutes.

Haunted Coop.name: Haunted Coop
Haunted Coop.disable: @Check[nature|dc:25] to recognize the unquiet animal spirits and soothe them, allowing the spirits to disperse
Haunted Coop.hazarddescription: A sudden flurry of shadowy pigeons erupts into a frenzy and breaks out of the coop.
Haunted Coop.reset: The haunted coop resets [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds} after it's triggered.

The Pigeons! The Pigeons!.name: The Pigeons! The Pigeons!
The Pigeons! The Pigeons!.description:
Trigger A person attempts to open the coop, searches the mounds within, or causes damage to it

Effect A sudden blast of shadowy pigeons emerges from the coop, shrieking and flapping into the face of the triggering creature anywhere they might be in the room. That creature must attempt a @Check[will|dc:27|options:inflicts:frightened] save with the following results.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and temporarily immune to these haunts for 24 hours.

Success The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}, and this frightened condition can't be reduced below 1 as long as they remain in area B2a.

Failure The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} and convinced that the pigeons are harbingers of a greater doom awaiting them. They cannot reduce their frightened condition below 1 for 24 hours.

Critical Failure As failure, but with an unlimited duration.

Consume Flesh.name: Consume Flesh
Consume Flesh.description:
Requirements The ghoul is adjacent to the corpse of a creature that died within the last hour.

Effect The ghoul devours a chunk of the corpse and regains @Damage[3d6[healing]] Hit Points.

It can regain Hit Points from any given corpse only once.

Ghoul Whispers.name: Ghoul Whispers
Ghoul Whispers.description:
Requirements A @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} creature is within the ghoul's reach

Effect The ghoul whispers dark thoughts and vile cravings into the creature's ears. The creature must save against the forbidden cravings curse.

Forbidden Cravings (curse) A creature can still eat and drink while sickened by this curse

Saving Throw @Check[will|dc:22|traits:curse]

Stage 1 carrier with no ill effects (1 day)

Stage 2 @Damage[2d6[void]] damage and the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} until it consumes raw meat (1 day)

Stage 3 as stage 2

Stage 4 as stage 2 unless the target has consumed raw meat in the past 24 hours, then it takes @Damage[4d6[void]] damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} until it consumes raw meat;

Stage 5 if the creature has eaten raw meat in the past 24 hours, it dies and rises as a ghoul, if not, it returns to stage 4

Grave Knowledge.name: Grave Knowledge
Grave Knowledge.description:
Frequency once per hour

Effect The ghoul calls upon knowledge it retains from one creature it has consumed in the past 7 days. The ghoul attempts a skill check using a skill in which the consumed creature was trained (if it's unclear whether the creature was trained, the GM decides). The ghoul is treated as trained and has a +13 skill modifier. This takes the same amount of actions or time as usual for the check.

The ghoul can instead automatically learn something specific known by a creature it consumed in the last 7 days, like the location of a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden} treasure or the name of a loved one. The ghoul can do this only once for a given creature, no matter how much of its flesh the ghoul consumed.

Swift Leap.name: Swift Leap
Swift Leap.description: The ghoul jumps up to half its Speed. This movement doesn't trigger reactions.

Join Us Forever.name: Join Us Forever
Join Us Forever.hp: moderate cover behind the bars from creatures outside the cell
Join Us Forever.disable: @Check[deception|dc:26] (trained) to trick one of the skeletons into thinking they're free, or @Check[religion|dc:23] (expert) to exorcise a haunted skeleton; each success disables one of the four haunted skeletons.
Join Us Forever.hazarddescription: The skeletal remains in the cells clatter up to their feet and reach out toward visitors as they call out, inviting them to embrace the addiction of imprisonment.
Join Us Forever.routine:
(4 actions) Each of the four skeletons targets a living creature in area C37, reaches their arms out toward the target, and in a mournful yet strangely compelling voice invites the target to join them in imprisonment forever, promising blissful enlightenment in return for an eternity spent behind bars. The skeletons attempt to target a different living creature, but if there are more skeletons than targets, they randomly target identical creatures. Targeted creatures must attempt a @Check[will|dc:26|options:damaging-effect,inflicts:paralyzed,inflicts:slowed,inflicts:stupefied] save, with a cumulative status penalty of –1 for each additional skeleton targeting them (to a maximum penalty of –3 if all four skeletons target a single creature), and the following results. This is an incapacitation and mental effect.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is tempted to remain in the room, takes @Damage[2d6[mental]] damage, and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} until the end of its next turn.

Failure The creature is compelled to remain in the room, takes @Damage[5d6[mental]] damage, and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed} until the end of its next turn.

Critical Failure The creature is compelled to remain in the room, takes @Damage[10d6[mental]] damage, becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} with an unlimited duration, and becomes paralyzed until the end of its next turn.
Join Us Forever.reset: The haunt deactivates at the end of any round in which there are no living creatures in the room. It then resets 1 minute later.

We've Been Here Forever.name: We've Been Here Forever
We've Been Here Forever.description:
Trigger A living creature ends their turn inside of area C37

Effect The skeletons rise up in a horrifying clatter. All living creatures in area C37 must attempt a @Check[will|dc:26|options:inflicts:paralyzed] save to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed} for 1 round (or 1 minute on a critical failure, with a new save at the end of their turn to recover). The haunt then rolls initiative.

Wrathful Armor.name: Wrathful Armor
Wrathful Armor.publicNotes:
Suits of animated armor see use both as guardians and as training partners in high-end martial academies able to afford the extravagance. Often, a warrior's old suit of armor can be turned into animated armor once it accrues too much battle damage to provide adequate protection. They're found most often in wizard laboratories and ancient dungeons.

Granted a semblance of life through the use of rituals or other strange magic, animated objects take many forms and serve a variety of uses. A few examples of typical animated objects are listed below. Many of these creatures serve as guardians, surprising unsuspecting adventurers when they suddenly attack. Others serve as idle distractions for the exceptionally rich, simple servants created to handle odd jobs, and the like.

Construct Armor (Hardness 9).name: Construct Armor (Hardness 9)
Construct Armor (Hardness 9).description: Like normal objects, an animated armor has Hardness. This Hardness reduces any damage it takes by an amount equal to the Hardness. Once an animated armor is reduced to less than half its Hit Points, or immediately upon being damaged by a critical hit, its construct armor breaks and its Armor Class is reduced to 13.

Soul Bolstering.name: Soul Bolstering
Soul Bolstering.description: When a suit of wrathful armor is destroyed, it falls to pieces and the soul energy that animated it redistributes to the remaining active suits, trailing prismatic energy and cries of pain as it goes. The first time this occurs, the soul flows into the three remaining suits, granting each suit 4 temporary HP. The second time this occurs, the soul flows into the two remaining suits, granting each 6 temporary HP. The third time this occurs, the soul flows to the one remaining suit, granting it 12 temporary HP. These temporary HP persist until they're lost or until they're replaced by a greater value of temporary HP.

Tetanus.name: Tetanus
Tetanus.description:
A creature that takes damage from a wrathful armor's glaive or gauntlet strike must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:14|traits:disease] save to resist contracting tetanus

Tetanus

Onset 10 days

Stage 1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} (1 week)

Stage 2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} and can't speak (1 day)

Stage 3 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed} with spasms (1 day)

Stage 4 death

Irrokcis Arudora.name: Irrokcis Arudora
Irrokcis Arudora.allSaves: +1 status to all saves vs. vitality

+1 Status to All Saves vs. Vitality.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Vitality

Arachnophobia.name: Arachnophobia
Arachnophobia.description: The first time in a round that a creature utilizes any spider-themed action in Irrokcis's presence (such as casting illusory creature to create a spider, or using summon animal to summon spiders), the lich becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 round from his horror. As long as a spider is visible to him (including a work of art, such as the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.c8v8gWJ87xiUVnsb]{Horrid Figurine} from area F14), he takes a –1 status penalty to saves against fear effects and loses steady spellcasting. The horrid figurine from area F14 is particularly effective if used against Irrokcis—increase that item's save DCs to 32 when they're used against the lich.

Rejuvenation.name: Rejuvenation
Rejuvenation.description: When a lich is destroyed, its soul immediately transfers to their @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.NEbr7nKuiluJgBHT]{Lich Soul Cage}. A lich can be permanently destroyed only if their soul cage is found and destroyed.

Drain Soul Cage.name: Drain Soul Cage
Drain Soul Cage.description:
7th rank

Frequency once per day

Effect The lich taps into their @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.qFVPeeJ70B1u2n81]{Soul Cage}'s power to cast any arcane spell up to the highest rank the lich can cast, even if the spell being cast is not one of the lich's prepared spells. The lich's soul cage doesn't need to be present for the lich to use this ability.

Reach Spell.name: Reach Spell
Reach Spell.description: If the next action Irrokcis takes is to Cast a Spell that has a range, increase that spell's range by 30 feet.

Siphon Life.name: Siphon Life
Siphon Life.description:
A lich's form draws forth life from those who come into contact with it. When the lich damages a living creature with an unarmed attack, the lich gains 5 temporary Hit Points and the creature must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:35|options:inflicts:drained] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1}.

If the lich is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} at the start of its turn, each creature grabbing or restraining it must succeed at a Fortitude save or become drained 1. If the lich siphons a creature's life again, the drained value increase by 1, to a maximum of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 4}.

Steady Spellcasting.name: Steady Spellcasting
Steady Spellcasting.description: As long as Irrokcis isn't in the presence of spiders, if a reaction would disrupt Irrokcis's spellcasting action, he attempts a @Check[flat|dc:15]. On a success, the action isn't disrupted.

Zizminarial.name: Zizminarial
Zizminarial.allSaves: +1 status to all saves vs. magic

Smell Prayers.name: Smell Prayers
Smell Prayers.description: Zizminarial is aware of divine magical items and active divine spells as a precise sense but cannot sense other types of magic at all.

+1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic

Ignite Soul.name: Ignite Soul
Ignite Soul.description:
Requirements Zizminarial is in area B12

Frequency once per round

Effect Zizminarial causes the flame of a burning candle to suddenly flare up. The soul within shrieks in pain as the fire lances out to burn a creature in area B12, who takes @Damage[4d6[fire]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:24|basic|options:inflicts:frightened] save; @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} on a failure or critical failure). The candle then burns out.

Residual Force.name: Residual Force
Residual Force.description:
Requirements The venedaemon's most recent action was to cast a spell

Effect Fading runes cling to the venedaemon's tentacles. The venedaemon makes a tentacle Strike that has a reach of 20 feet and deals 2d4 additional force damage.

Soul Spell.name: Soul Spell
Soul Spell.description:
If Zizminarial ingests a soul gem from a cacodaemon, he can recover an expended spell slot instead of gaining fast healing. The spell slot's rank can be no higher than half the level of the creature whose soul was consumed, rounded up.

Zizminarial can ingest a soul from one of the 22 candles burning in this room to regain a spell slot of any level; he cannot use a soul candle to gain fast healing, though.

Twisted Whispers.name: Twisted Whispers
Twisted Whispers.description:
The venedaemon whispers to a creature within 15 feet, which must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:24] save or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} for 1 minute (or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 3} on a critical failure).

Regardless of the results of the save, the creature is immune to Twisted Whispers for 24 hours.

Ilgrunthin.name: Ilgrunthin
Ilgrunthin.publicNotes:
The top half of a grindylow vaguely resembles a goblin, but from the waist down, their bodies split into a tangle of suckered, wriggling tentacles. Grindylows mostly dwell in shallow waters, fresh and briny, including lakes, rivers, coastal regions, and coral reefs. They generally organize into groups called schools, which can range from a few individuals to a few hundred. Smaller schools are sometimes taken over by a powerful aquatic creature, though such alliances only last until the school faces a major setback, at which point the surviving grindylows scatter and form smaller schools of their own.

Grindylows aren't territorial, but they are pragmatic. While they rarely build permanent structures, they will adopt a good hunting ground for generations until driven away by predators. They often lair in mobile shelters, such as a sargasso of seaweed or hull of an abandoned ship. They are skilled scavengers and hunters who eat anything they can sink their teeth into.

Grindylows respect the power of larger sea predators but have a special hatred for squids (or anything that resembles a squid). Sailors plying grindylow-infested waters often paint the images of squids on the bottoms of their hulls in hopes of warding off potentials raids. While this can keep smaller schools at bay, it can also backfire, potentially inciting larger groups to gather for a coordinated attack; this becomes especially likely if the ship's route is predictable. Their hatred of squids does not extend to other tentacled creatures; grindylows consider octopuses to be the epitome of grace and power.

equipment-Gold Ring set with Tiny Pearls.name: Gold Ring set with Tiny Pearls

Reactive Strike (Special).name: Reactive Strike (Special)
Reactive Strike (Special).description:
A grindylow gains 1 extra reaction at the start of each of their turns that they can use only to make a Reactive Strike with a tentacle. They can't use more than one Reactive Strike triggered by the same action or choice.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ReactiveStrike]

Clinging Suckers.name: Clinging Suckers
Clinging Suckers.description:
When a grindylow successfully @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.Tkd8sH4pwFIPzqTr]{Grabs} a creature larger than themself, they attach to that creature. The @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} creature is not @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized}, but if it moves, the grindylow moves with it.

If the creature is Medium or smaller, it takes a –5-foot status penalty to its Speeds while the grindylow is attached. The grindylow is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} while attached to a creature.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.FQX3YY3iFTtAtw1k]{Effect: Clinging Suckers}

Jet.name: Jet
Jet.description: The grindylow moves up to 60 feet in a straight line through the water without triggering reactions.

Aura of Doom.name: Aura of Doom
Aura of Doom.description: 30 feet. A living creature that enters the area must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:33|options:area-effect,inflicts:doomed] save or gain the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1} condition. A critical failure increases this condition to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 2}. Regardless of the result of the saving throw, the creature is temporarily immune to Velicarn's aura of doom for 1 minute.

Bastard's Shame.name: Bastard's Shame
Bastard's Shame.description:
Velicarn harbors deep feelings of shame and anger about his heritage, and a PC can capitalize on this to insult him or to distract him as follows.

Insult Velicarn The PC attempts a DC 30 Intimidation check to [[/act demoralize dc=30 options=inflicts:slowed]] Velicarn. On a critical success, he's also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} by his anger for 1 round. If he's also already @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} as a result of being distracted, he takes @Damage[6d6[mental]] damage (@Check[will|dc:30|basic] save) on a success (@Damage[12d6[mental]] damage on a critical success).

Distract Velicarn The PC attempts a DC 28 Deception check to [[/act feint dc=28 options=inflicts:slowed]] Velicarn. On a critical success, he's also slowed 1 by his anger for 1 round. If he's also already slowed as a result of being insulted, he takes @Damage[6d6[mental]] damage (@Check[will|dc:30|basic] save) on a success (@Damage[12d6[mental]] damage on a critical success).

Board Soul.name: Board Soul
Board Soul.description:
Trigger Velicarn reduces a creature to 0 HP with void damage

Effect Fragments of the creature's soul, manifesting as a vaguely spectral image of the creature, are pulled into the carriage and thereafter seen within, hammering silently on the windows while screaming to be rescued. A creature that dies while a fragment of its soul is trapped within the carriage can't become undead or be brought back to life until Velicarn is destroyed. A creature that's rescued before death is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} as long as part of its soul remains aboard the Black Coach.

Coin's Return.name: Coin's Return
Coin's Return.description:
A PC can toss @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.nBSlq58UkK86jYOO]{Velicarn's Cursed Coin}, or the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.2cWs7heYDt9jCSJ4]{Fortune's Coin} it becomes after it's uncursed, at the death coach as an Interact action whenever Velicarn is within 30 feet. Doing so causes the coin to vanish in a sudden flash. The coin is destroyed, and Velicarn must attempt a @Check[will|dc:35|options:damaging-effect,inflicts:off-guard,inflicts:stunned] save (@Check[will|dc:37|options:damaging-effect,inflicts:off-guard,inflicts:stunned] if the coin is no longer cursed) with the following results.

Critical Success Velicarn is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} until the start of his turn.

Success Velicarn takes @Damage[5d6[spirit]] damage and is off-guard until the start of his turn.

Failure Velicarn takes @Damage[10d6[spirit]] damage, is off-guard until the end of the PC's next turn, and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Critical Failure Velicarn takes @Damage[20d6[spirit]] damage, is off-guard for 1 minute, and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 3}.

Discorporation.name: Discorporation
Discorporation.description: If Velicarn is reduced to 0 Hit Points, the Black Coach and the two fiendish horses that drive it vanish immediately, and Velicarn transforms into a dullahan armed with a +2 greater striking astral battle axe. He falls @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} in a space of his choice previously occupied by the death coach and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 1 round. As soon as he ends a round without the slowed condition, he transforms back into a death coach and regains @Damage[100[healing]] Hit Points. Only by destroying him in his dullahan form before this (typically 2 rounds, unless his slowed condition is extended) can he be truly put to rest.

Site Bound.name: Site Bound
Site Bound.description:
Area C28

A typical ghost can stray only a short distance from where it was killed or the place it haunts. A typical limit is 120 feet. Some ghosts are instead bound to a room, building, item, or creature that was special to it rather than a location.

Rejuvenation.name: Rejuvenation
Rejuvenation.description: When a ghost is destroyed, it re-forms after [[/br 2d4 #days]]{2d4 days} within the location it's bound to, fully healed. A ghost can be permanently destroyed only if someone determines the reason for its existence and sets right whatever prevents the spirit from resting.

Compelling Order.name: Compelling Order
Compelling Order.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect Korven barks out an order at a creature within 30 feet, filling his command with humiliating insults and implied threats of punishment if the order is disobeyed, choosing from one of the following commands: "drop your weapons," "kneel," "stand at attention," or "pledge your loyalty." The target must attempt a @Check[will|dc:26] save with the following results, after which it is immune to Compelling Order for 1 minute.

Critical Success The creature can ignore the order; doing so causes Korven to sputter and rage, causing him to become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} on his next turn.

Success The creature resists the order but takes @Damage[4d6[mental]] damage as it does so.

Failure The creature is compelled to spend its first action on its next turn following the order, and also takes @Damage[8d6[mental]] damage from the shame.

Critical Failure The creature is compelled to spend its entire turn following the order, and takes @Damage[16d6[mental]] damage from the shame.

Phantom Amputation.name: Phantom Amputation
Phantom Amputation.description: Each time a creature takes damage in a round from the bloody tendril Strike extending from Korven's wrist, it believes its fingers, hand, or similar appendage has been amputated. The creature must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:26] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} on a critical failure). If the creature is already frightened, it instead becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} for 24 hours on a failed save (or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} for 24 hours on critical failure).

Sanctum Guardian.name: Sanctum Guardian
Sanctum Guardian.publicNotes:
Masters of mausoleums and keepers of crypts, the dread creatures called tomb giants are anathema to all living beings, but especially so to other types of giants. Long ago, so the legends say, tomb giants sold their souls in exchange for unfathomable power over the undead. Tomb giants construct massive gothic settlements in haunted valleys and on forsaken hillsides, far enough away from the societies of smaller people that they remain relatively undisturbed, but close enough that they can raid the graveyards of nearby villages with impunity. Elder tomb giants enjoy the thrill of subduing, slaying, and reanimating their fellow giants. A tomb giant views its mortal life as only one part of its existence. After death, most tomb giants are reanimated as undead, who then continue to practice their necromantic arts.

Spread across the world, giants are as diverse as the isolated places they inhabit. A giant makes a big impression on the local environment, especially on smaller and weaker creatures.

Dooming Touch.name: Dooming Touch
Dooming Touch.description: The tomb giant's claws carry the accursed power of their foul gods. A creature hit by the tomb giant's claw Strike becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1}.

Font of Death.name: Font of Death
Font of Death.description: The tomb giant turns the spiritual tide on a creature that has just died, temporarily transforming it into a volatile vessel powered by the Void. The tomb giant touches a creature that died within the past 24 hours, infusing its flesh and bone with void energy. Once during the next hour, the tomb giant can spend a single action (from any distance) to release this void from the corpse in an explosion that deals @Damage[10d8[void]|options:area-damage] damage in a @Template[type:burst|distance:15] (@Check[fortitude|dc:32|basic|options:area-effect] save); if not released before the end of the hour, the energy dissipates harmlessly. The tomb giant can't use Font of Death while a previous corpse remains infused.

Pallid Curse.name: Pallid Curse
Pallid Curse.description:
Frequency once per day

Trigger A sanctum guardian deals void damage on a creature within 30 feet

Effect The void damage scars the target's soul, infecting it with Urgathoa's presence. The target must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:32|options:inflicts:sickened] save with the following effects.

Critical Success The target suffers no additional effect.

Success The target becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} and gains weakness to void 5 until the end of its next turn.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.mJCiOTLp9eLxxsjb]{Effect: Pallid Curse (Success)}

Failure The target becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} and gains weakness to void 5; this weakness has an unlimited duration. If the target dies while this curse remains in effect, the curse ends, but the target automatically rises as an undead creature (the GM picks one of the same level as the target) that goes on to serve Urgathoa in its unlife. If the target is destroyed in its new undead form, it reverts to its original living form but is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yZRUzMqrMmfLu0V1]{Dying 3}.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.iZgvkZJ14Su7jWNE]{Effect: Pallid Curse (Failure)}

Critical Failure As failure, but weakness to void 10.

Jinnivere Arudora.name: Jinnivere Arudora
Jinnivere Arudora.allSaves: +1 status to all saves vs. magic

+1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic

Easy to Enrage.name: Easy to Enrage
Easy to Enrage.description:
Jinnivere still carries anger and frustration about the way her brother Augsten used to mercilessly tease her agility and lanky frame. A PC can attempt to insult her in the same way by making a special attempt to [[/act demoralize]] her with a @Check[intimidation|dc:24] check, with the following results.

Critical Success The insult cuts deep. Jinnivere loses the effects of her Head Hunter ability and Frightful Presence for the next hour, becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} on her next turn as she spends one of her actions sputtering and seething in anger. The DC for her to Command an Animal on her mount rises to DC 28. The next attempt to enrage her using this insult by any PC gains a +4 circumstance bonus to the Intimidation check.

Success Jinnivere sputters with anger at the insult and loses the effects of her Head Hunter ability and Frightful Presence until the end of her next turn. On her next turn, she focuses her attacks on the insulting PC (unless a different PC achieves this result before her turn, in which case her anger shifts to that PC). The next attempt to enrage her using this insult by any PC gains a +2 circumstance bonus to the Intimidation check.

Failure As success, but Jinnivere retains her Head Hunter ability and no circumstance bonus is granted.

Critical Failure Jinnivere is annoyed but not otherwise bothered by the insult. The PC who critically failed the check cannot attempt to enrage her in this way again for 1 minute.

Agonizing Welts.name: Agonizing Welts
Agonizing Welts.description:
Jinnivere can wield her riding crop as a melee weapon to create agonizing pain in the minds of those she strikes. It also inflict a curse that causes their mental pain to manifest as painful visible welts and seeping wounds that never seem to heal. If she inflicts agonizing welts on a creature already afflicted by it, the victim attempts a new save, ignoring the result if it's better than a failure.

Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:26]

Stage 1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} (1 round)

Stage 2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} and all speeds are reduced by 10 feet (1 round)

Stage 3 As stage 2, except @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 3} (1 round)

Stage 4 As stage 2, except clumsy 3 and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} (1 round)

Head Hunter.name: Head Hunter
Head Hunter.description: Any slashing weapon gains the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.hg3IogR8ue2IWwgS]{Keen} rune while a dullahan wields it, and any hatchet they wield gains the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.qlunQzfnzPQpMG6U]{Returning} rune as well. If the dullahan kills a creature with a critical hit using a slashing weapon, the target is decapitated as though the dullahan had used Reap on the target.

Reap.name: Reap
Reap.description: The dullahan removes the head of a dead creature within reach. Each creature within the area of the dullahan's frightful presence must attempt a new save, even if it is temporarily immune.

Summon Steed.name: Summon Steed
Summon Steed.description: The dullahan summons a war horse with elite adjustments and the fiend and unholy traits. This steed remains until it is slain, the dullahan Dismisses this effect, or the dullahan Summons a Steed again.

It's Never Enough.name: It's Never Enough
It's Never Enough.disable: @Check[survival|dc:28] (trained) to draw upon memories of leaner times and counteract the temptation of the promised meal or @Check[religion|dc:31] (expert) to exorcise the haunt; 2 successes are required to disable it, and once the haunt is disabled, the food on the table is revealed to be foul, rotting, and moldy.
It's Never Enough.hazarddescription: The smells and sights of fresh baked goods compel those who experience them to take part in a grisly feast.
It's Never Enough.routine:
(1 action; mental) On its initiative, the haunt exudes mental compulsions to all living creatures in the room, driving them to take part in the offered feast. Each living creature in the room must attempt a @Check[will|dc:26|traits:mental] save with the following results. Food consumed during this hazard's routine is automatically replenished at the start of the next round.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is compelled to approach the table of food and be seated. On the creature's turn, it Strides as often as needed to reach the table, then Interacts with a chair to be seated. If it has any remaining actions, it can use them normally (such as by Interacting again to stand up from being seated at the table).

Failure As success, but the creature must spend at least one of its actions this turn (if any are available after potentially approaching and taking a seat) Interacting with the food to eat some of it. Eating the food afflicts the creature with Rancid Breakfast.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature must use any actions not used to approach the table or be seated at it to Interact and eat food.
It's Never Enough.reset: The haunt deactivates at the start of any round in which there are no living creatures in area D2, then reactivates 1 minute later.

Break Your Fast.name: Break Your Fast
Break Your Fast.description:
Trigger A living creature enters area D2

Effect The sight and scent of the baked goods grows nearly irresistible. The triggering creature must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:26|options:inflicts:stupefied] save to avoid becoming @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} on a critical failure) for 24 hours. The hazard then rolls initiative.

Rancid Breakfast.name: Rancid Breakfast
Rancid Breakfast.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:26|options:damaging-effect,inflicts:clumsy] (this increases to @Check[fortitude|dc:28|options:damaging-effect,inflicts:clumsy] if a creature spent two actions eating or @Check[fortitude|dc:30|options:damaging-effect,inflicts:clumsy] if a creature spent three actions eating)

Stage 1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} (1 round) and @Damage[1d6[poison]]

Stage 2 clumsy 1 (1 hour) and @Damage[2d6[poison]]

Stage 3 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} (24 hours) and @Damage[4d6[poison]]

Stage 4 clumsy 2 (unlimited duration) and @Damage[6d6[poison]]

Bound to Bastardhall.name: Bound to Bastardhall
Bound to Bastardhall.description: Unlike the typical phantom, Shirail exists fully in the Ethereal Plane and cannot shift back and forth between this plane and the Universe.

–1 Status Penalty to All Saves vs. Death.name: –1 Status Penalty to All Saves vs. Death

Bound Even in Death.name: Bound Even in Death
Bound Even in Death.description: As phantom, but if Shirail is reduced to 0 Hit Points by any means, her soul does not return to the River of Souls. Instead, her soul is drawn into the soul vortex in the vault under Bastardhall (area I).

Physical Manifestation.name: Physical Manifestation
Physical Manifestation.description: Upon reaching rank 1, Shirail manifests a semi-physical body. She loses the incorporeal trait, her immunities and resistances, and her fly Speed, and gains a land Speed of 25 feet. She has a Strength modifier of +2, an Athletics modifier of +9, an AC of 21, 75 HP, and divine innate spells. Her other statistics do not change.

Phantom Touch.name: Phantom Touch
Phantom Touch.description: Each time they make a Strike, a phantom can choose to deal spirit damage instead of the normal physical damage type.

Spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
Spellcasting.description:
Once Shirail is rank 1 and has a physical body, she gains the following divine innate spells. As her rank increases, her occult spell DC and spell attack modifier increase, and she gains additional innate spells.

Divine Innate Spells DC 22, attack +14; 3rd @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.SUKaxVZW2TlM8lu0]{Cleanse Affliction}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.rfZpqmj0AIIdkVIs]{Heal}; 2nd @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.SUKaxVZW2TlM8lu0]{Cleanse Affliction}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.rfZpqmj0AIIdkVIs]{Heal}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Et8RSCLx8w7uOLvo]{Sound Body}; 1st @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.qXTB7Ec9yYh5JPPV]{Cleanse Cuisine}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.rfZpqmj0AIIdkVIs]{Heal}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.yHujiDQPdtXW797e]{Spirit Link}; Cantrips (3rd) @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.gpzpAAAJ1Lza2JVl]{Detect Magic}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.qwZBXN6zBoB9BHXE]{Divine Lance}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.WBmvzNDfpwka3qT4]{Light}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.OhD2Z6rIGGD5ocZA]{Read Aura}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.kcelf6IHl3L9VXXg]{Vitality Lash}

Rank 2 DC 24, attack +16; 4th @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.SUKaxVZW2TlM8lu0]{Cleanse Affliction}; 3rd @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.LQzlKbYjZSMFQawP]{Locate}. Her cantrips are heightened to 4th rank.

Rank 3 DC 26, attack +18; 5th @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Et8RSCLx8w7uOLvo]{Sound Body}; 4th @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.ikSb3LRGnrwXJBVX]{Vital Beacon}. Her cantrips are heightened to 5th rank.

Scarecrow's Leer.name: Scarecrow's Leer
Scarecrow's Leer.description:
40 feet.

The scarecrow's eyes flicker with an unnerving glow. A creature can't reduce its @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened} condition below 1 as long as it is in the aura's emanation. When a creature enters or starts its turn in the aura, it must attempt a @Check[will|dc:27] save. Living creatures made of flesh take a -2 circumstance penalty to this save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and is then temporarily immune for 24 hours.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AdPVz7rbaVSRxHFg]{Fascinated} by the scarecrow until the end of its next turn.

Critical Failure As failure, but @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3}.

Baleful Glow.name: Baleful Glow
Baleful Glow.description: The scarecrow's head bursts into ghostly, heatless flame that sheds bright light in a @Template[emanation|distance:20] (and dim light to the next 20 feet). If the scarecrow uses this ability on the first round of combat, any creature that has not acted yet is startled and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} against the scarecrow for 1 round. It can suppress the light by using this action again.

Mundane Appearance.name: Mundane Appearance
Mundane Appearance.description: Until it acts, the taxidermy allosaurus resembles an ordinary (if well-crafted) taxidermy creature. It has an automatic result of 43 on Deception checks and DCs to pass as an ordinary taxidermy display.

Thrashing Tail.name: Thrashing Tail
Thrashing Tail.description: The taxidermy allosaurus smashes furniture and displays in the area with its tail, spreading the resulting rubble around. A 5-foot by 15-foot area of your choice that has at least one square adjacent to the creature becomes difficult terrain. If this area includes the stone tub, the acid splashes out and the difficult terrain becomes hazardous terrain as well that deals @Damage[1d6[acid]] damage.

Toothsome Fear.name: Toothsome Fear
Toothsome Fear.description: The taxidermy allosaurus's strikes deal an additional 2d6 mental damage to frightened creatures.

Sahkil Imp.name: Sahkil Imp
Sahkil Imp.publicNotes: Imps are fiendish infiltrators and corrupters who, despite their diminutive stature, are more than capable of subtly influencing a weak-willed individual into performing increasingly evil acts over time. An imp will often agree to serve a mortal and act docile and loyal in a long-term plot to eventually get their master killed or damn their soul. Imps are born directly from the Outer Planes themselves, rather than from mortal souls, and thus they serve outside any fiendish hierarchies, granting them leeway to pursue their specialties. Despite standing a mere 2 feet tall, imps can be vicious combatants, flying out of reach and turning invisible to escape should the odds turn against them.

Change Shape.name: Change Shape
Change Shape.description:
The imp takes on the appearance of a Medium or smaller animal. While transformed, the imp loses their normal senses, innate spells, and special actions, but doesn't otherwise change their statistics and can still speak and use telepathy. The imp also gains any special senses of the animal and any Speeds the animal has.

This doesn't change the attack and damage modifiers of their Strikes but might change the damage type their Strikes deal (depending on what kinds of attacks the animal has) and prevents them from exposing creatures to imp venom.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ChangeShape]

Fiendish Healing.name: Fiendish Healing
Fiendish Healing.description:
Frequency once per round.

Effect The imp regains @Damage[1d6[healing]] Hit Points.

Fiendish Temptation.name: Fiendish Temptation
Fiendish Temptation.description:
Frequency once per day

Effect The imp offers a nonfiend within 15 feet a bargain, granting a boon of good luck if the creature accepts voluntarily. The boon lasts for 1 hour once accepted.

Once during the hour, the creature can roll an attack roll or saving throw twice and use the higher result. If the creature dies while the boon is in place, the imp decides where the creature's soul travels. This typically makes the soul bound for eternity in the imp's home plane, and the creature unable to be raised or resurrected except by the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.6dDtGIUerazSHIOu]{Wish} ritual or similar magic.

Imp Venom.name: Imp Venom
Imp Venom.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:16]

Maximum Duration 6 rounds

Stage 1 @Damage[1d6[poison]] damage and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} (1 round)

Stage 2 @Damage[1d6[poison]] damage, clumsy 1, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} (1 round)

Aznithakantus.name: Aznithakantus
Aznithakantus.allSaves: +1 status to all saves vs. vitality

Bardic Lore.name: Bardic Lore
Bardic Lore.description: Sphinxes are naturally curious, and their love of puzzles and mysteries leads them to gather information on a broad range of topics. Sphinxes have Bardic Lore, a special Lore skill that can be used only to Recall Knowledge, but on any topic.

Rejuvenation.name: Rejuvenation
Rejuvenation.description: When Aznithakantus is destroyed, the energies of the Bastardhall Curse rebuild her body on the steps of the onyx ziggurat over [[/gmr 1d10 #days]]{1d10 days}; if her body is destroyed during that time, the process starts as new. She can be destroyed permanently if the Bastardhall Curse is lifted.

+1 Status to All Saves vs. Vitality.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Vitality

Blindingly Flammable.name: Blindingly Flammable
Blindingly Flammable.description: 30 feet. Aznithakantus's leathery undead flesh is infused with strange reagents. Whenever she takes fire damage, the fire flares blindingly bright, and any creature in the aura's area must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:30] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} for 1 round (or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} for 1 minute on a critical failure); this is a visual effect. When she takes persistent fire damage, these flames leap out and burn any creature in the aura for an equal amount of damage (@Check[reflex|dc:30|basic] save).

Claw Rake.name: Claw Rake
Claw Rake.description: The sphinx rears back on their hind legs and makes two claw Strikes at the same target, using the same attack bonus as their highest melee attack. If both attacks deal damage, the target takes extra damage equal to one claw Strike.

Gift of Dust.name: Gift of Dust
Gift of Dust.description:
Requirements Aznithakantus's last action was a successful claw Strike

Effect Dust from Aznithakantus's claw seeps into the wound, infecting the target with painful aches as the flesh around the wound grows gray and begins to flake away in dusty chunks. The creature takes @Damage[5d8[void]] damage with a @Check[will|dc:24|basic|options:inflicts:stunned] save. If the creature critically fails the saving throw, it becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 3}.

Pounce.name: Pounce
Pounce.description: The sphinx Strides and makes a Strike at the end of that movement. If the sphinx began this action @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden}, they remain hidden until after the attack.

Riddler's Rune.name: Riddler's Rune
Riddler's Rune.description:
Once per week, a Sphinx can create a magical symbol as the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.o0l57UfBm9ScEUMW]{Rune Trap} ritual. The sphinx usually shapes it to take the form of a written riddle and sets the password to the answer.

A creature that gives the wrong answer or tries to pass without answering must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:33] save or be affected by one of the following spells, chosen by the sphinx when creating the symbol: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.BilnTGuXrof9Dt9D]{Synaptic Pulse} (7th), @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.vLA0q0WOK2YPuJs6]{Charm} (7th), @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.4koZzrnMXhhosn0D]{Fear} (7th), @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.R8bqnYiThB6MYTxD]{Phantom Pain} (7th), @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.o4lRVTwSxnOOn5vl]{Sleep} (7th). The sphinx learns the identity of any creature that answers the riddle and tends to be friendly to them if they answered correctly.

Mirrosight.name: Mirrosight
Mirrosight.description: As long as Madam Skerzana holds a hand mirror, she can see through the mirror with darkvision and the effects of truesight. She's blind when she isn't holding a mirror.

Light Sickness.name: Light Sickness
Light Sickness.description: A stygira in an area of bright light is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}.

Mirror Gaze.name: Mirror Gaze
Mirror Gaze.description:
Madam Skerzana holds aloft her antique silver mirror and gazes through it into the past or future of a creature within 30 feet, infusing its thoughts with visions of their helplessness as a new-born baby or of a potential death from violence or peril in the future. Madam Skerzana chooses if she's showing the past or the future when she uses Mirror Gaze. The targeted creature must attempt a @Check[will|dc:26] save or become affected as indicated below, depending on which vision Madam Skerzana chose to impart.

The Past A glowing green eye momentarily opens on the right side of Madam Skerzana's face, and the target creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} on a critical failure) as their mind reverts to a limited infantile intellect. At the end of the character's turn, the value of this stupefied condition decreases by 1.

The Future A glowing blue eye momentarily opens on the left side of Madam Skerzana's face, and the target creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} on a critical failure) as their mind reels from a harrowing vision of their imminent death. Describe this death vision to the PC briefly, choosing one of the Arudoras that the party has yet to encounter and defeat. When that PC encounters that Arudora later in the campaign, they must attempt a new @Check[will|dc:26|options:inflicts:frightened] save to avoid becoming frightened 1 (frightened 2 on a critical failure) all over again.

Stone Curse.name: Stone Curse
Stone Curse.description: Wounds dealt by the stygira's claws leave the flesh bleached of color and turn the blood that runs from them dark gray. Each time a creature is damaged by the stygira's claw Strike, it must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:26] save or become permanently @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 2} on a critical failure) as its flesh stiffens like stone. If a creature is reduced to 0 Hit Points from the stygira's claw Strike and fails the saving throw against stone curse, it's petrified. A creature that spends 8 hours in direct sunlight can attempt a new saving throw to remove the effects of stone curse, even if it has been petrified.

Site Bound.name: Site Bound
Site Bound.description: These three ghosts can only leave the crypts when Bastardhall appears on Golarion, and even then, they can't leave the island.

Rejuvenation.name: Rejuvenation
Rejuvenation.description: The three adventurers re-form after [[/gmr 2d4 #days]]{2d4 days} here in the crypts unless someone carries their respective urn of ashes down to the temple in Maiserene (area A9) to be cleansed by Shirail.

Jazlin's Haunted Arrows.name: Jazlin's Haunted Arrows
Jazlin's Haunted Arrows.description:
Jazlin manifests a shortbow and fires a ghostly, shrieking arrow at a target he can see within 30 feet. The target must attempt a @Check[will|dc:28] save with the following results.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes @Damage[2d6[spirit]] damage.

Failure The target takes @Damage[4d6[spirit]] damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Critical Failure The target takes @Damage[8d6[spirit]] damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3}.

Malevolent Possession.name: Malevolent Possession
Malevolent Possession.description: The ghost attempts to possess an adjacent corporeal creature. This has the same effect as the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.wU6hNzK8Yfqdmc8m]{Possession} spell (@Check[will|dc:23]), except since the ghost doesn't have a physical body, it is unaffected by that restriction of the spell.

Middenworm Infestation.name: Middenworm Infestation
Middenworm Infestation.disable: @Check[medicine|dc:23] or @Check[thievery|dc:26] to carefully cut into the corpse and vent the worms harmlessly in a safe direction
Middenworm Infestation.hazarddescription: A dead body seems to ripple and bulge, as if something inside were shaking.

Worm Burst.name: Worm Burst
Worm Burst.description:
Trigger A creature jostles or touches the infested corpse

Effect The corpse bursts open, spraying hundreds of middenworm larvae in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:20]. Creatures in the area must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:25|options:area-effect,damaging-effect,inflicts:sickened] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} and takes @Damage[2d8[piercing]|options:area-damage] damage from worm bites.

Failure The creature is sickened 1 and takes @Damage[4d8[piercing]|options:area-damage] damage plus @Damage[2d6[persistent,piercing]|options:area-damage] damage as the biting worms latch on.

Critical Failure As failure, but @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} and the persistent piercing damage increases to @Damage[4d6[persistent,piercing]|options:area-damage] damage.

Velicarn's Head (Haunt).name: Velicarn's Head (Haunt)
Velicarn's Head (Haunt).disable: @Check[religion|dc:30] (expert) to exorcise the haunt; three successes area required to disable it
Velicarn's Head (Haunt).hazarddescription: A hideous mound of flesh, shattered bone, tangles of hair, and what appears to be gray matter lies in a glistening, 2-foot-tall heap on the floor, only to suddenly start piling up on itself to gradually form an immense, hateful head.
Velicarn's Head (Haunt).routine: (1 action) On its turn, Velicarn's head continues to grow and expand as it becomes a monstrous distortion of his once-human appearance, with beady red eyes, sharp fangs, and two bat-like wings that unfurl from either side. The haunt screeches louder, and all creatures in the library take @Damage[4d6[persistent,bleed]] damage as blood pours from their ears, eyes, and mouths (@Check[fortitude|dc:28|basic] save). If Velicarn's head isn't disabled or destroyed by the end of the third round, it rips out of the ground and joins the fight as a horrific monstrosity—a daqqanoenyent. At this point, the haunt is automatically disabled, and the PCs must face this new threat. As a daqqanoenyent, Velicarn's head focuses its attacks on the PCs and ignores the sahkil (who, if still alive, titters and cackles in delight at this development). It pursues PCs relentlessly and fights until it's destroyed, which permanently destroys the hazard.
Velicarn's Head (Haunt).reset: Velicarn's head collapses back into a 2-foot-high mound of gore at the end of any round in which no non-fiend living creatures are in the library. It then resets 1 minute later.
Velicarn's Head (Haunt).stealthdetails: (master) to notice the mound of gore is haunted; noticing the mound itself has a DC of 0

Awakened Horror.name: Awakened Horror
Awakened Horror.description:
Trigger A living non-fiend creature approaches within 15 feet of the remains of Velicarn's head

Effect The mound of gore shudders and quakes, then starts to pile up on itself, slowly transforming into an immense, screaming head. All living creatures in area F1 must attempt a @Check[will|dc:28|options:inflicts:frightened] save as the gurgling birth-shriek of the awakening horror tears through the room. Those who fail become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} on a critical failure). The haunt then rolls initiative.

Aron Mordimus.name: Aron Mordimus
Aron Mordimus.allSaves: –1 status penalty to all saves vs. death effects

Bound to Bastardhall.name: Bound to Bastardhall
Bound to Bastardhall.description: Unlike the typical phantom, Aron exists fully in the Ethereal Plane and cannot shift back and forth between this plane and the Universe.

–1 Status Penalty to All Saves vs. Death.name: –1 Status Penalty to All Saves vs. Death

Bound Even in Death.name: Bound Even in Death
Bound Even in Death.description: As phantom, but if Aron is reduced to 0 Hit Points by any means, his soul does not return to the River of Souls. Instead, his soul is drawn into the soul vortex in the vault under Bastardhall (area I).

Physical Manifestation.name: Physical Manifestation
Physical Manifestation.description: Upon reaching rank 1, Aron manifests a semi-physical body. He loses the incorporeal trait, his immunities and resistances, and his fly Speed, and gains a land Speed of 25 feet. He has a Strength modifier of +0, an Athletics modifier of +7, an AC of 21, 80 HP, and Pour Elixir. His other statistics do not change.

Phantom Touch.name: Phantom Touch
Phantom Touch.description: Each time they make a Strike, a phantom can choose to deal spirit damage instead of the normal physical damage type.

Pour Elixir.name: Pour Elixir
Pour Elixir.description:
Requirements Aron has a physical body

Frequency twice per day

Effect Aron forms a pitcher in one hand from ectoplasm, then pours liquid from the pitcher out onto a solid surface. As the liquid pours, it forms into a single glass vial filled with an alchemical elixir of Aron's choice. He's always willing and eager to Pour an Elixir for the PCs when asked. An elixir created by this ability vanishes if not used within 24 hours of being poured. He can choose from the following options when he uses Pour Elixir: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.AJ1dC7EtTIfBey0M]{Moderate Antidote}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.biRbqKo2C97XLfQ0]{Moderate Antiplague}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.Y8115p3cmQJBqk5d]{Moderate Darkvision Elixir}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.lPcnDlBGz5QwCMYw]{Moderate Eagle Eye Elixir}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.TZUskLT7yvP7N2co]{Lesser Elixir of Life}.

Rank 2 Aron's elixirs are now greater versions rather than moderate (or in the case of an elixir of life, a moderate one instead of a lesser one).

Rank 3 Aron can now Pour Elixir three times a day, and his elixirs of life are now greater elixirs of life.

Voldrak.name: Voldrak
Voldrak.publicNotes:
It seems like every lake in Ustalav of any considerable size has its own legend about a lake monster, but in the case of Lake Laroba, these legends have been fact for as long as anyone can remember. The lake's denizen, Voldrak, was only rarely sighted in the days before the curse, despite entire expeditions of hopeful monster-watchers spending extensive hours on the lake.

Now, like all other creatures swept up by the Bastardhall Curse, Voldrak has grown worse. The lake monster torments anyone who dares ply the waters for too long. He generally prefers to frighten or maim rather than kill, for this new Voldrak enjoys the knowledge that his horrific legend might spread.

Voldrak is a sleek, plesiosaur-like serpent, with four clawed flippers, deep-red eyes, and a long tail that ends in a single long rudder-like fin. His teeth are long and terrible and protrude over his lips even when his mouth is closed.

Voldrak's Fate

Before the curse, Voldrak was an elusive @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core-2.Actor.ZdQfNuQQjytFzuyd]{Water Orm} regarded by the Arudoras almost as a mascot or pet to such an extent that they worked his image into their family crest. After the curse, though, Voldrak became a much more aggressive and dangerous monster. While he's unlikely to survive the events of Bastion of Blasphemies, Lake Laroba is deep, and who's to say the lake monster's ghost doesn't survive in its depths after the PCs return home?

Dread Gaze.name: Dread Gaze
Dread Gaze.description:
Voldrak fixes his gaze upon a creature he can see within 60 feet. His eyes glow with blue light, then begin to pulse, compelling the creature he views to remain motionless with fear. The target must attempt a @Check[will|dc:36|options:inflicts:frightened,inflicts:slowed,inflicts:paralyzed] save with the following effects. Voldrak can't use Dread Gaze again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Dread Gaze]]{1d4 rounds}.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune to Dread Gaze for 24 hours.

Success The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The creature increases the value of its frightened condition by 1 (or becomes frightened 1 if not yet frightened). As long as the creature remains frightened, it is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 2}.

Critical Failure As failure, but as long as the creature remains frightened, it is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed}.

Maimed But Alive.name: Maimed But Alive
Maimed But Alive.description: If Voldrak would kill a creature with damage from his bite or tail Strike, he can opt instead to reduce the creature to 1 Hit Point and maim it, causing the creature to become permanently @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 3} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 3} (Voldrak's choice) from the horrific wound.

Toxic Spit.name: Toxic Spit
Toxic Spit.description: Voldrak spews a @Template[type:line|distance:60] of toxic sludge, dealing @Damage[8d6[poison]|options:area-damage] damage to all creatures in the area (@Check[fortitude|dc:36|basic|options:area-effect] save).
